Appriss Retail publishes no public developer API program — its APIS Online portal is an authenticated Asset Protection Information System (customer login), not a developer API surface.

providers.name: Boise Cascade
providers.description: Boise Cascade is a leading North American manufacturer and distributor of building materials for the residential and commercial construction industry. The company produces engineered wood products (EWP) including I-joists, LVL beams, and glulam, as well as structural panels and lumber, and distributes a broad range of building materials through its wholesale distribution network.

providers.name: LS Retail
providers.description: LS Retail provides modular point‑of‑sale (POS) and business management software solutions for retail, hospitality, and other industries. Their flagship LS Central platform integrates POS, inventory, e‑commerce, and analytics, enabling seamless operations across stores, restaurants, hotels, pharmacies, and forecourts. LS Retail serves global brands with cloud‑enabled, Microsoft Dynamics‑based solutions, offering extensive customization, scalability, and support for omnichannel experiences.

providers.name: Kitterly
providers.description: Kitterly, Inc. was a direct-to-consumer craft commerce startup that sold knitting and crochet kits, yarn, needles and notions online, and ran a monthly Kit Club subscription that shipped members a pattern plus the yarn required to complete it. Kitterly was backed by 500 Global (500 Startups) along with Manatt Ventures and the Jordan x 2080 accelerator. The company was later consolidated under the Cotton Cuts brand, a Chesterfield, Missouri based quilting fabric shop selling designer die-cut and pre-cut fabric, threads, patterns and notions, plus quilting memberships and the Puzzle Mystery Quilt program, serving roughly 4,000 members across more than 15 countries. The kitterly.com domain now redirects to cottoncuts.com. The business is a consumer retail and subscription commerce operation running on a hosted e-commerce platform, and it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Storefront
providers.description: Storefront (thestorefront.com) is an online marketplace for renting short-term commercial retail space, connecting brands, e-commerce businesses, and artists with space owners to launch pop-up shops, showrooms, galleries, product launches, and events. The platform lists tens of thousands of spaces across 50+ cities in North America, Europe, and Asia, with flexible day/week/month rentals and a secure booking-and-payment flow, 24-hour support, and a Priority Pass membership. Storefront was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal (api.thestorefront.com is private/401), so this profile captures company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: ANN Inc.
providers.description: ANN Inc. is the former parent company of Ann Taylor and LOFT, specialty retailers of women's apparel, shoes, and accessories. ANN Inc. was acquired by Ascena Retail Group in 2015 and subsequently sold to Sycamore Partners in December 2020 for $540 million, alongside Lane Bryant and Lou & Grey brands. The brands now operate under KnitWell Group (formerly Premium Apparel LLC), a Sycamore Partners holding company that also owns Talbots. Ann Taylor and LOFT offer affiliate programs for digital publishers.

providers.name: KoRo
providers.description: KoRo (KoRo Handels GmbH) is a Berlin-based direct-to-consumer food retailer that sells nuts, dried fruit, nut butters, snacks, protein products, baking ingredients and drugstore goods in bulk packaging at wholesale-style prices, shipping across Europe from country storefronts in Germany (korodrogerie.de), Austria, Switzerland, France, Italy and the Benelux/EU shop at koro.com. Founded in 2014 and backed by HV Capital and Partech, KoRo runs a headless commerce stack — a Shopware 6 backend fronted by a Nuxt storefront deployed on Vercel — and publishes its engineering work as open source through the KoRoHandelsGmbH GitHub organization, including a Nitro-based Shopware Store-API proxy and several Shopware 6 build-tooling packages on npm under the @korodrogerie scope. KoRo publishes no public developer portal, no documented partner or commerce API, and no API specifications; its Store-API surface is internal and gated behind per-sales-channel access keys.

providers.name: Walgreens Boots Alliance
providers.description: Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) is a global pharmacy-led health and wellbeing enterprise operating in more than 25 countries, with pharmacy chains Walgreens in the US and Boots in the UK, pharmaceutical wholesale and distribution through Alliance Healthcare, and specialty pharmacy operations. WBA operates as a Fortune 100 company and global healthcare platform, leveraging data science, AI, and digital health technologies to serve patients, customers, and health systems. While WBA's primary developer APIs are offered through the Walgreens Developer Program, the enterprise also uses healthcare data platforms for population health management, specialty pharmacy integration, and digital health services.

providers.name: ARVI SA
providers.description: ARVI SA operates a premium online wine shop offering a curated selection of over 5,000 fine and rare wines from renowned regions such as Bordeaux, Burgundy, and Tuscany. Based in Switzerland, the company provides secure shipping and 24‑hour delivery throughout the country. Customers can browse an extensive catalog, filter by producer, vintage, price, and region, and purchase directly through the website. The platform emphasizes high‑quality service, authenticity guarantees, and a seamless shopping experience for wine enthusiasts and collectors.

providers.name: Atolls
providers.description: Atolls (formerly Global Savings Group) is a Munich-based consumer commerce-content company that operates the world's largest shopping engagement platform, running coupon, cashback, deals, and shopping-community destinations across more than 20 markets. Its brand portfolio includes Coupons.com, Cuponation, iGraal, Shoop, Pouch, mydealz, hotukdeals, and Deala, connecting millions of shoppers with offers from thousands of retailers and brands through affiliate marketing, cashback, and AI-enhanced shopping insights. Founded in 2012 as CupoNation with Rocket Internet and rebranded to Atolls in 2024, it is backed by investors including HV Capital, RTP Global, and Rocket Internet. Atolls publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI document or SDK — api., developer. and docs.atolls.com do not resolve — but it does serve real machine-readable documents: RFC 9116 security.txt files on five owned hosts pointing at a single group-wide Intigriti vulnerability disclosure program, and OpenID Connect discovery documents on seven Pepper community properties (mydealz, hotukdeals, Dealabs, Preisjaeger, Chollometro, Pepper PL, Promodescuentos) that expose an OAuth 2.0 authorization server for consumer sign-in. This profile captures that security, identity, and legal surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Innoviti
providers.description: Innoviti Technologies Pvt. Ltd. is a Bengaluru-based payment technology company and RBI-authorized payment aggregator (online and, since January 2026, in-store) operating under India's Payment & Settlements Act 2007. Founded in 2002, Innoviti builds collections, reconciliation, and revenue-assurance infrastructure for large organized retail. Its products include innoviti unipay (an enterprise payment and reconciliation platform for omnichannel settlements and leakage control), innoviti genie (a sales acceleration and dealer-margin platform for mobile and electronics retail), and innoviti link (a POS-free mobile collection app accepting cards, UPI, and EMI). The company serves enterprise retailers including Samsung, Reliance Retail, Tanishq, Shoppers Stop, and More Retail, holds multiple payment-communication patents, and maintains PCI DSS, PCI P2PE, and PCI PIN certifications. Added to the API Evangelist network as a fintech portfolio lead; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or self-serve API documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Minoan
providers.description: Minoan is a hospitality procurement and shoppable-stays platform. Short-term-rental hosts, property managers, hotels, and interior designers source furniture, decor, and home goods at insider/trade pricing through Minoan's purchasing platform, and earn revenue share when guests buy the items they experienced during a stay. Founded to turn every hosted space into a shoppable showroom, Minoan connects properties to hundreds of home-and-lifestyle brands and handles sourcing, checkout, and fulfillment. Backed by Accel. As of this profile Minoan exposes no public developer API; this record captures its public web, security, and llms.txt surface.

providers.name: Nfinite
providers.description: Nfinite (formerly Hubstairs) is a visual intelligence platform for the digital shelf. It helps consumer brands and retailers automatically analyze, generate, and monitor compliant product visuals — detecting visual compliance gaps across every retailer and brand and fixing them at scale using AI-generated 3D and synthetic product imagery. The product is delivered as a web application (my.nfinite.app) rather than a public developer API; no OpenAPI, developer portal, or published documentation exists at the time of enrichment. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Our Place
providers.description: Our Place is a direct-to-consumer kitchenware and cookware brand, best known for the multi-purpose Always Pan, selling cookware, bakeware, appliances, tableware, and kitchen tools at fromourplace.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc, its digital storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a native agentic-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) shopping endpoint, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect authentication, and an agent-facing llms.txt / agents.md. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the company's live public agent surface.

providers.name: SyncSpider
providers.description: SyncSpider provides eCommerce automation and integration tools for online shops, multivendor marketplaces, and brick‑and‑mortar stores. It enables businesses to sync inventory, orders, and product data across platforms, offering a universal API layer that simplifies complex integrations and streamlines operations for retailers and partners.

providers.name: Max Retail
providers.description: Max Retail is a Techstars-backed platform that helps brick-and-mortar boutiques and multi-location retailers turn unsold and aged inventory into cash. Retailers connect their point-of-sale or e-commerce system — Shopify, RICS, or Square — or upload a CSV, and Max Retail lists, markets, and sells the items to a network of shoppers across multiple channels, handles customer service, and pays out through Stripe when a prepaid shipping label is scanned. The retailer only ships; Max Retail charges a flat 15% fee plus shipping. Max Retail integrates inbound with third-party commerce platforms and payment processors but does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a webhook surface of its own.

providers.name: Tory Burch
providers.description: Tory Burch LLC is an American luxury women's fashion label founded in February 2004 by designer Tory Burch and headquartered in New York City, trading under the legal entity River Light V, L.P. The privately held company designs and sells ready-to-wear clothing, designer shoes, handbags, small leather goods, jewellery, watches, eyewear, fragrance and beauty, swimwear and home decor, together with the Tory Sport activewear line, through roughly 400 boutiques worldwide, wholesale partners and a direct-to-consumer storefront at toryburch.com serving the United States, United Kingdom, the European Union and Asia. Its affiliated Tory Burch Foundation funds and educates women entrepreneurs. Tory Burch is a fashion and retail business rather than a software vendor: it operates no developer program, publishes no API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contract, and holds no public GitHub organisation. Its storefront is a Next.js front end on Akamai over a Salesforce Commerce Cloud (Demandware) commerce platform with Adobe Scene7 media, and an Apigee API gateway fronts www.toryburch.com/api/ for first-party storefront traffic only, exposing no publicly registered proxy. The one machine-readable artifact the company does publish is a site-wide llms.txt.

providers.name: Unicorn Auctions
providers.description: Unicorn Auctions is a Chicago-based online auction marketplace for rare spirits and fine wine, founded in 2019 by A.J. Heindel, Cody Modeer and Phil Mikhaylov out of the city's restaurant and bar trade. Every lot is sold on consignment: Unicorn authenticates, appraises, photographs and digitizes each bottle before listing it in one to three weekly online auctions that can carry several thousand lots spanning bourbon, scotch, Japanese whisky, tequila, agave spirits and wine. The company also runs a bonded vault storage service for collectors, and publishes The Unicorn Review, an editorial and auction-intelligence blog. Bidding is entirely digital, through the web platform and native iOS and Android apps. Unicorn Auctions publishes no public developer program - no OpenAPI, SDK, webhook catalog or developer portal - and the api.unicornauctions.com backend that serves its own clients is private, undocumented and disallowed in robots.txt.

providers.name: Fetch
providers.description: Fetch (formerly Fetch Rewards) is a consumer rewards and loyalty platform that lets shoppers earn points by scanning receipts and shopping at more than 600 partner brands in-store and online, playing mobile games, and redeeming offers, then exchange those points for gift cards to retailers such as Amazon, Target, and Uber. Its Fetch for Business arm turns verified purchase data into full-funnel brand engagement, consumer spending insights, and campaign tooling (including the Fetch Ad Manager) for CPG, retail, restaurant, and agency partners. Fetch is a private, venture-backed company; it operates a consumer mobile app plus a Chrome extension and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Proudly
providers.description: Proudly is a direct-to-consumer baby care brand, co-founded by Dwyane Wade and Gabrielle Union, that centers the unique skin and hair needs of Black and Brown babies to make products better for all. Its Shopify-hosted storefront sells skincare (balms, washes, oils), hair care, baby wipes, absorbent diapers, bath and body kits, apparel and gift bundles under a "No Sketchy Stuff" ingredient-transparency commitment. Backed by Initialized Capital (via A-Frame Brands), Atacama Ventures and VMG Partners. Proudly is a consumer commerce company with no public developer API or SDK program; the only machine surface is its Shopify Customer Account OpenID/OAuth well-known configuration.

providers.name: AiFi
providers.description: AiFi is a spatial-intelligence platform that uses camera-only computer vision to understand human behavior in physical spaces. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, it powers autonomous checkout, frictionless identity and entry, real-time fraud prevention, historical journey analytics and an operational co-pilot across retail, stadiums and arenas, quick-service restaurants, travel hubs, healthcare, campuses and government border control. The platform needs no shelf sensors or RFID and tracks shoppers with anonymous skeletal keypoint detection rather than facial recognition by default. AiFi publishes a suite of retailer-facing OASIS APIs that bridge its platform to POS (NCR, Oracle, Square) and payment (Stripe, Adyen) systems, but the developer documentation is served only to authenticated accounts through an AiFi Keycloak single sign-on.

providers.name: Brandback
providers.description: Brandback is a Berlin-based embedded resale infrastructure company (legal entity Arbor Technologies GmbH) that lets online retailers and fashion brands integrate resale directly into their baskets, product listings, and checkouts. Shoppers see an item's future resale value before they buy, resell it later in a single click, and receive store credit, while Brandback's AI handles pricing recommendations, condition checks, customer service, shipping, disputes, and payouts. Retailers can launch a white-label resale marketplace with no upfront cost and integrate with any e-commerce platform. Founded in 2023 and backed by $7.4M in pre-seed and seed funding led by Earlybird VC, Brandback reports a 9.5% average conversion-rate lift with customers including Replay Jeans and Sandqvist.

providers.name: Enplug
providers.description: Enplug is a cloud-based digital signage and content-management platform that powers communications on screens across retail, hospitality, corporate, and public-venue locations, with content apps for social feeds, dashboards, video, wayfinding, and menus managed from a central web dashboard. Enplug was acquired by Spectrio, and enplug.com now redirects to Spectrio's Enplug acquisition page; the legacy Enplug cloud login remains live at login.enplug.com. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; Enplug exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this repo carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Cladwell
providers.description: Cladwell is a smart-closet and outfit-planning consumer application that helps people build capsule wardrobes and get more wear out of the clothes they already own. The service digitizes a user's closet, then uses AI styling ("Ask Cladwell") together with weather and personal preferences to recommend daily outfits, reduce over-buying, and encourage sustainable, intentional dressing. With more than one million app downloads, Cladwell is delivered primarily as iOS/Android and web apps (app.cladwell.com) with a subscription model; it currently exposes no public developer API. Founded and led by CEO Erin Flynn, it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Gap
providers.description: Gap Inc. is a Fortune 500 American clothing and accessories retailer operating the Gap, Old Navy, Banana Republic and Athleta brands. Gap Inc. publishes no public developer API, no machine-readable contract and no developer portal: probing found an Apigee gateway at api.gap.com that exposes no proxy to an anonymous caller, and a dangling developer-portal CNAME at developer.gap.com (gap-api-docs-portal.apigee.net) whose service is gone and whose TLS certificate does not cover the hostname. What Gap does publish is a HackerOne vulnerability disclosure programme and one first-party open-source Android HTTP library. This repository is an independent third-party profile of that public surface.

providers.name: Kafene
providers.description: Kafene is a New York-based point-of-sale financing platform that lets retailers offer transparent lease-to-own (LTO) purchase options to prime and non-prime consumers. Founded in 2019 by Neal Desai and James Schuler, the company underwrites shoppers with an AI-driven risk model that pulls 20,000+ data points to return an approval — up to $5,000 — in seconds, then pays the merchant directly on delivery confirmation while the customer pays weekly or biweekly until ownership. Merchants originate applications from their in-store POS or by sending a text-to-apply link; consumers manage leases and payments in a self-service dashboard. Kafene raised a ~$31M Series B and reaches merchants through financing-waterfall networks such as Versatile Credit and LendPro. As of the 2026-08-01 enrichment probe Kafene publishes no public developer program, no OpenAPI/GraphQL/MCP contract, no SDKs, and no /.well-known discovery surface; its merchant and consumer surfaces are authenticated single-page web applications and integration is arranged through Kafene's partner team, not self-serve documentation.

providers.name: Lenskart
providers.description: Lenskart is a direct-to-consumer eyewear company operating an omnichannel retail business across prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, contact lenses and eye-care services. It sells through localized storefronts (India, United States, Singapore and other markets) and mobile apps, and merchandises its own house brands including Vincent Chase, John Jacobs, Lenskart Studio and Lenskart Boost alongside third-party labels. The digital experience layer includes 3D/AR virtual try-on and look comparison, a saved-prescription and prescription-history profile, order tracking and a loyalty program. Lenskart is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. As of this enrichment pass Lenskart publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition or client SDKs; the developer- and docs-named subdomains that resolve are gated behind Cloudflare and return 403 to unauthenticated clients, so no API surface could be verified.

providers.name: Poshmark
providers.description: Poshmark is a social commerce marketplace where people in the US, Canada, Australia and India buy and sell new and secondhand fashion, accessories, home goods, beauty products, and electronics. Sellers list items from their closets, share and cross-promote listings across the community, host live selling shows, and ship using prepaid labels while Poshmark handles payments and buyer protection. Founded 2011, IPO 2021, acquired by Naver in 2023. Poshmark runs a consumer web and mobile marketplace backed by internal APIs but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Harmonya
providers.description: Harmonya is a New York- and Tel Aviv-based product intelligence company for consumer packaged goods manufacturers and retailers. Founded in 2021, it reads live product listings, pack and label copy, manufacturer specs, syndicated feeds and consumer reviews, and turns them into normalized product attributes at the UPC level — claims, ingredients, flavors, pack, dietary positioning and measured nutrition values — plus demand themes and consumer-voice signals layered on top. The platform ships as four modules (Demand Intelligence, Consumer Intelligence, Attribute Intelligence and Product Catalog) delivered through a tenant web application at app.harmonya.com and as an enriched product feed into a customer's PIM, data lake and analytics stack. Harmonya publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract; access runs through a sales conversation and an Auth0-protected tenant.

providers.name: BabyList
providers.description: Babylist is the leading universal baby registry and a baby-focused commerce and content company for growing families. Because the registry is universal, parents can add any product from any store — including Amazon, Target, and Etsy — to a single list. Babylist has grown into a full ecosystem spanning the Babylist registry, the Babylist Shop, Babylist Health (insurance-covered breast pumps), Babylist Money (family financial planning), expert product guides, and a flagship Los Angeles showroom. More than 10 million people shop with Babylist every year. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network; Babylist runs no public developer API, but it does publish an llms.txt agent surface and an OpenID Connect discovery document.

providers.name: nChannel
providers.description: nChannel is a SaaS integration platform that empowers retailers and wholesalers to synchronize data across eCommerce, ERP, POS, and 3PL systems. It automates processes such as order fulfillment, inventory synchronization, and supply chain management, providing a unified hub for seamless data flow between disparate business applications.

providers.name: Serve First
providers.description: Serve First is a UK-based AI-driven customer experience (CX) platform that unifies reviews, surveys, receipts, in-location feedback terminals, operational audits, and mystery shopping into a single dashboard. It turns real-time customer feedback into role-based, actionable insight, with sentiment analysis and unified reporting across retail, hospitality, facilities management, health & wellness, and franchise businesses. Serve First also provides Client Connect journey/workflow automation and Martyn's Law public-protection compliance management. Serve First does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; this profile captures company identity plus verified security and compliance posture (SOC 2 and ISO 27001 via a Sprinto-hosted trust center).

providers.name: CommerceIQ
providers.description: CommerceIQ is an AI-powered ecommerce platform that helps consumer brands win in algorithmic retail across sales, digital shelf, retail media, and content execution. Its unified platform, Ally AI, packages four AI agents (Content, Shelf, Media, and Sales) that optimize product content and SEO, monitor digital-shelf availability and search rankings across 1,450+ retailers globally, manage and automate retail media bidding and spend, and forecast and execute sales strategy from Amazon and Walmart to Instacart and Criteo. Founded in 2019, CommerceIQ serves enterprise brands including PepsiCo, P&G, Coca-Cola, and Colgate-Palmolive, and is backed by Insight Partners, SoftBank Vision Fund, and Trinity Ventures. The company operates as a managed enterprise platform and does not publish a public self-service API or developer portal.

providers.name: CQuotient
providers.description: CQuotient is the artificial intelligence and shopper-data technology that powers personalization and predictive commerce for Salesforce B2C Commerce (Commerce Cloud) Einstein. Originally an independent commerce-personalization startup, CQuotient was acquired by Demandware in 2013, and Demandware was in turn acquired by Salesforce in 2016. Today the CQuotient engine underpins Einstein product recommendations, predictive sort, Einstein search dictionaries, and shopper activity capture. Its developer surface is the Salesforce B2C Commerce Einstein API (also referred to as the CQuotient API), documented within the Salesforce Developers documentation rather than on a standalone CQuotient portal.

providers.name: Join
providers.description: Join (Join Stories, join-stories.com) is an AI video commerce platform that helps e-commerce brands create, distribute, and measure short-form video across their sales channels. Its products include shoppable video embedded on product and collection pages, user-generated content (UGC) activation from social media, video analytics with A/B testing, an AI Studio that generates video and images from product data, and interactive web stories. Deployment is a single embed snippet with native integrations for Shopify, PrestaShop, Magento, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, WooCommerce, and headless storefronts. The company is backed by Canaan Partners and Seedcamp.

providers.name: Ernesta
providers.description: Ernesta is a direct-to-consumer, custom-sized rug company that lets homeowners and interior-design professionals order high-design rugs made to measure down to the inch. Founded by three Peloton co-founders (John Foley, Hisao Kushi, and Yony Feng) and backed by True Ventures, Addition, and Platform Capital, Ernesta sells online through a Shopify storefront and a growing set of showrooms, and runs a dedicated Trade Program and Trade Portal for designers. Ernesta publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile catalogs the company's consumer and trade web properties plus the discovery, security, and identity signals observable on its public hosts.

providers.name: Livsn Designs
providers.description: Livsn Designs is a Techstars-backed outdoor apparel brand that makes durable, minimalist technical clothing (its Flex Canvas pants and multi-use travel and hiking apparel) sold direct-to-consumer from a Shopify storefront at livsndesigns.com. It publishes no first-party developer API or documentation portal. Its only programmatic surface is the agent-commerce layer Shopify serves on the merchant's own domain: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) shopping MCP endpoint for agent-driven checkout, a Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth2 authorization server, and an llms.txt / agents.md agent-instructions document. This profile captures that real agent surface; there is no bespoke API to catalog.

providers.name: Agreable
providers.description: Agreable (아그레아블) is a South Korean direct-to-consumer brand-commerce company founded by Lim Seung-jin (임승진, "Jason Im") out of a reading-club community of the same name. It has run the frozen convenience-food platform Wingeat (윙잇, wingeat.com) since 2015, and in March 2022 renamed itself after that brand — the operating legal entity is now 주식회사 윙잇 (Wing Eat, Inc.) in Guro-gu, Seoul, and agreable.com and agreable.co.kr both redirect to career.wingeat.com. The company designs, contract-manufactures and fulfils its own private-label food brands — 윙잇Dining, 윙잇Made, 고른, 페이보잇, 랠리 and 방아당 — across more than 200 products. It is a consumer packaged-goods and retail operator, not a software vendor: it builds its storefront, ERP and fulfilment systems in house on private hosts and publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDK, no machine-readable specification and no agent surface of any kind. Its GitHub organization, wingeat-inc, carries zero public repositories.

providers.name: Leflair
providers.description: Leflair is a Vietnamese online retail brand selling discounted authentic international brands across fashion and accessories, beauty and health, home and lifestyle, and children's products. Its own terms of service describe it as Vietnam's first members-only flash-sale platform, running daily promotional events on branded goods. The live storefront at leflair.com is operated by Cong ty TNHH Sopa Technology of Ho Chi Minh City on the Haravan commerce platform, and is supported by a Vietnamese-language editorial blog, an account/sign-in surface, and published terms, privacy, payment-security, shipping, and tax policy pages. Leflair is a consumer retail brand: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer portal, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API definition, and its historical leflair.vn domain no longer serves the storefront. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: The Coca-Cola Company
providers.description: The Coca-Cola Company is the world's largest non-alcoholic beverage company, owning and marketing more than 200 brands across sparkling soft drinks, water, hydration, sports, coffee, tea, juice, dairy, and plant-based drinks. The company sells its products in more than 200 countries through a bottling and distribution partner network. While Coca-Cola does not currently publish a broadly available public REST API, it is a heavy enterprise API consumer running an internal API program on MuleSoft that connects ERP, manufacturing, distribution, retail, marketing, and consumer engagement systems through a Center for Enablement (C4E) model. Historical Coca-Cola Enterprises (CCE) Product and Location APIs at developer.cokecce.com are no longer maintained as a public-facing developer program.

providers.name: Atoms
providers.description: Atoms is a direct-to-consumer footwear brand founded in 2019 by Waqas Ali and Sidra Qasim and headquartered in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, New York. The company designs, develops, and sells minimalist everyday sneakers - notably its Model 000 and Model 001 lines - and differentiates itself with quarter-size sizing and the ability to buy a pair in two different sizes for each foot. Product features include lightweight foam cushioning, a copper-infused antimicrobial lining, stretch slip-on laces, and an 8mm heel-to-toe drop. Atoms sells online via a Shopify storefront and is backed by Initialized Capital, Kleiner Perkins, DST Global, and Serena Ventures. It has no public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Freshop
providers.description: Freshop is an eCommerce platform purpose-built for grocery and specialty retail, now part of NCR Voyix. It powers branded online storefronts, mobile shopping, order fulfillment, pickup, and delivery for independent and regional grocers, and integrates third-party services for loyalty, coupons, email, SMS, and fulfillment. Freshop exposes a live REST API at api.freshop.com that serves store and product data to Freshop-powered storefronts and apps, authenticated with an application key (app_key) query-string parameter and versioned by a numeric path segment.

providers.name: Garmentory
providers.description: Garmentory is a Seattle-based online fashion marketplace that connects shoppers with more than 1,000 independent boutiques and emerging designers across 30+ countries. Backed by Techstars, the platform curates apparel, accessories, and footwear from independent retailers, letting boutiques list inventory manually or sync it through a Shopify integration. Garmentory runs a heavily customized Spree Commerce (Ruby on Rails) storefront and consumes third-party APIs (payments, retail media, and merchant onboarding) rather than publishing a first-party public developer API. This profile tracks Garmentory's identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network; no OpenAPI, developer portal, or API reference is published at this time.

providers.name: Josh Wood Colour
providers.description: Josh Wood Colour is a UK-based at-home hair colour brand founded by celebrity colourist Josh Wood, selling permanent and semi-permanent hair dye, root touch-up, gloss, toners, blonde and grey-blending products, and haircare direct to consumers through a Shopify-powered online store at joshwoodcolour.com. The brand pairs its retail catalogue with a free personalised colour-matching consultation service and editorial hair-care advice. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer retail e-commerce brand it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface; this profile captures its web identity, security posture, and customer-facing properties.

providers.name: Merchbar
providers.description: Merchbar, Inc. is the official merchandise retailer for top musicians, selling vinyl records, CDs, t-shirts, hoodies, posters, and other band merchandise across thousands of artist storefronts at merchbar.com. It runs a consumer shopping experience alongside a "Merchbar for Artists" program and official merchandise integrations with YouTube and Spotify. Merchbar is a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital. As of this enrichment pass Merchbar publishes no public API, developer program, SDKs, or technical documentation — no developer/api/docs subdomain resolves and there is no /.well-known/security.txt — so this profile captures only its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Rent-A-Center
providers.description: Rent-A-Center is a lease-to-own retail company providing furniture, electronics, appliances, and computers through its Rent-A-Center stores and Acima (formerly AcceptanceNOW) in-store kiosk program. Headquartered in Plano, Texas, Rent-A-Center operates thousands of stores across the United States, Mexico, and Puerto Rico. The company's technology platform supports online store management, customer account self-service, lease agreement processing, and the Preferred Lease virtual store integration program for retail partners. No public developer API is currently documented. The Acima platform provides a lease-to-own integration capability for partner retailers via a separate developer program.

providers.name: Sesh
providers.description: Sesh (Sesh Products US, Sesh+) is an Austin, Texas consumer packaged goods company that manufactures and sells tobacco-free nicotine pouches. Products ship in multiple flavors (Mint, Wintergreen, Clear, Mango, Cappuccino, Raspberry Lemon) and strengths (4mg, 6mg, 8mg), sold direct-to-consumer via subscription and through 5,000+ retailers. Surfaced as an 8vc portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable developer surface — this is a physical-goods brand running on a Shopify storefront, so the profile carries identity and domain-security only.

providers.name: Spoiler Alert
providers.description: Spoiler Alert is a Boston-based software company (a Techstars portfolio company) that helps consumer packaged goods (CPG) manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers manage and sell excess, short-dated, and obsolete inventory. Its purpose-built platform digitizes discounting and liquidation processes, matching surplus inventory with the right buyers at the right price through a secondary marketplace, with automated listing generation, dynamic pricing optimization, freight cost management, and performance analytics to recover margin and reduce food and product waste. The platform is delivered as a closed SaaS application (app.spoileralert.com); no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: Lovepop
providers.description: Lovepop is a Boston-based consumer greeting-card and gifting company, founded in 2014 and known for its intricate laser-cut 3D pop-up cards inspired by Vietnamese "kirigami" paper engineering. The company sells directly to consumers through its Shopify-powered storefront at lovepop.com and through retail partners, offering pop-up greeting cards, gift boxes, flowers, and personalized gifting. Lovepop was accelerated by Techstars and appeared on ABC's Shark Tank. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; as of this pass Lovepop publishes no first-party developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, and its public digital surface is a standard Shopify commerce storefront (including Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth well-known documents served on the domain).

providers.name: Property Capsule
providers.description: Property Capsule (PropertyCapsule) is a retail and commercial real estate marketing automation and prospecting platform for landlords and brokers. It centralizes property, tenant, and availability data in one place and automatically publishes it as flyers, tourbooks, interactive site plans, aerials, demographics, and competition maps across web and iPad leasing apps. Founded around 2014, the company was acquired by VTS in October 2019 and its capabilities were folded into the VTS Market product. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures.

providers.name: Serena & Lily
providers.description: Serena & Lily is a California home furnishings and lifestyle brand founded in 2003 in Sausalito by textile designer Serena Dugan and entrepreneur Lily Kanter. It sells furniture, custom upholstery, bedding, rugs, lighting, wallpaper, art and home decor direct to consumers through its e-commerce site, a printed catalog, and a network of physical Design Shops, alongside a Designer Circle trade program for interior designers. The storefront runs on a headless, composable commerce stack — Elastic Path for commerce and Amplience for content, served from a Vercel-hosted front end in front of AWS AppSync and Amazon API Gateway — but Serena & Lily publishes no developer program, no public API documentation, and no machine-readable specification of any kind. The GraphQL endpoint backing the storefront answers anonymous requests with introspection disabled, and the api.serenaandlily.com gateway rejects every unauthenticated path.

providers.name: The House Of LR&C
providers.description: The House of LR&C (Love, Respect & Care) is a Seattle-based, mission-driven direct-to-consumer fashion company founded in 2020 by Russell Wilson, Ciara, and retail veteran Christine Day. A Certified B Corporation, it operates a portfolio of apparel brands including Good Man Brand, LITA by Ciara, and Human Nation, donating 3% of net revenue to the Why Not You Foundation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Its public commerce runs on Shopify; the company publishes no first-party developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. The only machine-readable surface on the storefront host is Shopify's platform-level Customer Account API OIDC discovery document.

providers.name: buynomics
providers.description: Buynomics is a Cologne, Germany-based software company providing an AI-powered Revenue Growth Management (RGM) platform for consumer goods, retail, telecom, and consumer software companies. Its proprietary "Virtual Shoppers AI" runs agent-based simulations of consumer purchasing behavior so commercial teams can optimize pricing, promotions, price pack architecture (product mix), and trade terms before going to market — capturing cross- effects, cannibalization, and competitive response. The platform's Decision Guide generates prescriptive recommendations from thousands of evaluated scenarios. Buynomics is used by brands including Unilever, Nestle, L'Oreal, Danone, General Mills, Vodafone, and Ferrero, and is backed by Insight Partners and Seedcamp. The product is delivered as a web application; no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is published at this time.

providers.name: Highstock
providers.description: Highstock is a private, AI-native wholesale marketplace that connects consumer brands holding excess or unsold inventory with a vetted network of global business buyers. Focused initially on beauty and personal care, the platform lets brands convert surplus stock into cash while protecting brand value and channel privacy, and gives buyers access to authentic inventory directly from brands at exclusive pricing, with centralized order management and flexible payment terms. The company reports 50+ beauty and personal care brands, 100+ wholesale buyers, $100M+ in listed inventory, and more than 1M pounds of product diverted from landfill, with offices in New York (US) and Gurgaon (India). Highstock does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead for enrichment.

providers.name: Teespring
providers.description: Teespring is a creator-commerce and print-on-demand platform, founded in 2011, that lets creators design, launch, and sell custom apparel and merchandise with no upfront cost or inventory, handling production, payment, and fulfillment on the creator's behalf. Backed by a16z, the company rebranded to "Spring" in 2021 and now operates as Amaze Commerce (part of Amaze Holdings): its consumer storefront lives at spri.ng while the creator/merchant SaaS platform runs at amazecommerce.com and amaze.co. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, /.well-known discovery surface, or llms.txt; this profile therefore captures verified company identity and published site properties only.

providers.name: Primary
providers.description: Primary (Primary Kids, Inc.) is a direct-to-consumer children's apparel brand selling simple, slogan-free, mix-and-match clothing "in all colors, for all kids" — babies through age 14, plus adult sizes, swimwear, school uniforms and licensed Sesame Street collaborations. The company operates a Shopify-hosted online store at primary.com and is a portfolio company of Homebrew. Primary has no first-party developer API, but its storefront is agent-accessible: it serves a live hosted Shopify Storefront MCP server (catalog search, product lookup, cart, checkout, policy/FAQ lookup) and exposes Shopify's Customer Account API (OAuth2/OIDC) for customer-scoped operations, along with a published llms.txt agent-instructions document.

providers.name: Astro Sea
providers.description: Astro (PT Astro Technologies Indonesia), operating at astronauts.id, is an Indonesian quick-commerce platform that delivers groceries and everyday essentials in as little as 15 minutes. Its consumer mobile apps (iOS and Android) offer more than 3,000 curated products spanning fresh produce, frozen goods, groceries, beauty, household items, and electronics, with 24/7 service across the Greater Jakarta (JADETABEK) region. Astro is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was surfaced through that portfolio into the API Evangelist network. Astro is a business-to-consumer application company; it publishes a consumer app, a corporate site, and an RFC 9116 security contact, but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: CAKE POS
providers.description: CAKE POS provides a cloud‑based point‑of‑sale (POS) platform designed for restaurants and retail businesses. It offers tools for order management, payment processing, inventory tracking, employee scheduling, and analytics, all accessible via web and mobile interfaces. The service integrates with popular payment gateways and third‑party services, enabling seamless operations for small to medium‑size enterprises seeking modern, scalable POS solutions.

providers.name: Matsmart
providers.description: Matsmart (operating internationally as Motatos) is a Swedish e-commerce company that fights food waste by selling surplus, short-dated, and overstocked groceries and household goods at a discount, with average savings of up to 50%. Its catalog spans pantry staples, beverages, snacks, candy, baby food, health and beauty, cleaning supplies, pet food, and non-food surplus, sourced from manufacturers and retailers and shipped across Sweden and other European markets via partners including Bring, Airmee, and PostNord. The company runs a consumer web storefront and iOS/Android apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API or documentation, so this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: Cheaf
providers.description: Cheaf is a mobile food-rescue marketplace that connects supermarkets, restaurants, bakeries, and food retailers holding surplus inventory with consumers who buy it as discounted "surprise packages" at pickup, cutting food waste while helping merchants recover value on stock that would otherwise be thrown away. Founded in Mexico in 2020, the consumer app operates across Mexico, Chile, and Argentina, has more than 3.5 million users, and reports millions of kilograms of food rescued and greenhouse-gas emissions avoided. Businesses list surplus through a merchant onboarding portal and pay a commission on sales; consumers browse and reserve packages through the mobile app. This API Evangelist profile tracks Cheaf's public web and developer surface; Cheaf is a consumer/merchant mobile platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: Dollar Shave
providers.description: Dollar Shave Club is a direct-to-consumer men's grooming and personal-care brand founded in 2011 and acquired by Unilever in 2016, best known for pioneering the subscription razor model that ships blades, shave butter, skincare and body-care products to members on a recurring schedule. The company sells through its own e-commerce storefront (dollarshaveclub.com, built on Shopify) as well as retail channels, offering razor handles and cartridges, grooming kits and gift sets. It surfaces in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. Dollar Shave Club does not operate a public developer program or documented API; its digital surface is a consumer Shopify storefront whose only machine-discoverable interface is Shopify's customer-account OAuth/OIDC (including a customer-account MCP API scope) exposed at the store's /.well-known/ discovery endpoints.

providers.name: Grove Collaborative
providers.description: Grove Collaborative is a digital-first consumer products company and online marketplace for sustainable everyday household essentials — eco-friendly cleaning supplies, bamboo and recycled paper products, personal care, beauty, pet, and vitamins & supplements from hundreds of vetted brands. Orders meet strict ingredient standards and are carbon neutral, and the company operates as a plastic-neutral, sustainability-focused retailer sold through grove.co (a Shopify-hosted storefront) and retail partners. Grove is a public benefit company (NYSE: GROV) that was an early portfolio company of 500 Global and Bullpen Capital. It publishes no first-party developer API or public developer program; this profile captures its public web, security, and Shopify-platform discovery surface.

providers.name: Reflex Careers
providers.description: Reflex (Reflex Careers) is an on-demand labor platform for retail stores, connecting brands and store operators with vetted, background-checked associates for short-notice shift coverage. The platform handles employer-of-record responsibilities including payroll, tax withholding, and compliance, lets retailers post shifts with as little as two hours' notice, and uses a two-way review system to build worker track records and brand-specific training per shift. Reflex serves retail brands including Ariat, Faherty, Fossil, and Everlane and is backed by Canaan Partners. Added to the API Evangelist network from the Canaan Partners portfolio; as of this enrichment pass Reflex publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Saysh
providers.description: Saysh is a direct-to-consumer athletic footwear and apparel brand founded by Olympic champion sprinter Allyson Felix, designing sneakers engineered specifically for women's biomechanics under the banner "Women Deserve Better." Its lineup spans performance running shoes (the Felix Runner and Evelyn Runner) and the everyday Saysh One, plus apparel, accessories, and the Saysh+ Run Club membership. The saysh.com storefront runs on Shopify, so customer-facing commerce is served through the Shopify platform rather than a first-party Saysh developer API; no public Saysh API program, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal were found. Backed by Redpoint Ventures.

providers.name: FIGS
providers.description: FIGS, Inc. (NYSE: FIGS) is a founder-led, direct-to-consumer healthcare apparel and lifestyle brand founded in 2013 by Heather Hasson and Trina Spear and headquartered in Santa Monica, California. FIGS designs and sells premium scrubwear and non-scrubwear offerings — lab coats, underscrubs, outerwear, footwear, compression socks, loungewear, and accessories — directly to healthcare professionals through its Shopify-based online store at wearfigs.com. FIGS is a consumer e-commerce and retail brand with a customer help center and investor-relations presence; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: KupiVIP
providers.description: KupiVIP (kupivip.ru) is a Russian online outlet retailer for luxury and premium fashion, selling women's and men's apparel, footwear, bags, accessories and home goods from more than 250 international designer brands at discounts of up to 90% on previous-season collections. The 1C-Bitrix storefront ships across Russia, publishes a 100% authenticity guarantee backed by expert verification, offers free delivery on orders over 30,000 RUB, and runs telephone, email, WhatsApp and Telegram customer support. The company was originally surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Accel portfolio company. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment probe KupiVIP publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: NuORDER
providers.description: NuORDER by Lightspeed is a global B2B commerce platform for wholesale buying and selling between brands and retailers. It combines a fully-branded wholesale eCommerce storefront with account-specific pricing and discounts, an Assortments planning tool for data-driven buying and reduced markdowns, and a Marketplace that connects buyers to 3,000+ brands across fashion, footwear, and apparel. NuORDER exposes a partner-gated REST API at api.nuorder.com for syncing products, orders, catalogs, and customer data with ERP, PIM, and other commerce systems. Acquired by Lightspeed in 2021, it is used by brands including Arc'teryx, Kendra Scott, TOMS, Barbour, and Canada Goose.

providers.name: Ross Stores
providers.description: Ross Stores, Inc. (NASDAQ: ROST) is the largest off-price apparel and home fashion retailer in the United States, operating over 1,700 Ross Dress for Less and 320+ dd's DISCOUNTS stores across 43 states, the District of Columbia, and Guam. The company sources a broad assortment of in-season, name-brand merchandise at deep discounts (20-60% below department and specialty store prices) through opportunistic buying. Ross operates a highly efficient supply chain powered by AI-driven inventory management, distribution automation, and integrated supplier and partner technology platforms.

providers.name: Dick's Sporting Goods
providers.description: DICK'S Sporting Goods is a Fortune 500 omni-channel sporting goods retailer selling sports equipment, apparel, footwear and accessories across the DICK'S, House of Sport, Golf Galaxy, Public Lands and Going Going Gone banners. It publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract: the storefront is an Angular single-page app that answers HTTP 200 with the same shell for every path, and neither api. nor developer.dickssportinggoods.com resolves in DNS. Its B2B integration surface is X12 EDI over AS2/SFTP through third-party trading networks, with vendor guidelines handed out as PDFs. The company does run a named Vulnerability Disclosure Program on Bugcrowd.

providers.name: Adentro
providers.description: Adentro (formerly Zenreach) is a WiFi marketing and customer-intelligence platform that connects online marketing spend to real-world, in-store visits for brick-and-mortar businesses. Branded guest-WiFi portals capture and enrich first-party customer profiles, measure foot traffic and a "Walk-Through Rate" attribution metric, and power automated email and audience-targeting campaigns across roughly 100 million verified US consumer profiles. Adentro serves retail, food and beverage, venues and arenas, and entertainment and hospitality brands. It exposes a partner/customer-gated Contacts API and a Location & Scanning API (V2/V3) for syncing captured contacts, visits, and location data into CRMs and loyalty platforms such as Fishbowl and Alpine IQ; access is granted via an Adentro-issued token passed in the Authorization header rather than through a public self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: BloomNation
providers.description: BloomNation is a flower-delivery marketplace that connects consumers with independent local florists for same-day and next-day delivery of handcrafted floral arrangements across 40+ U.S. cities and the UK. Customers shop florist-designed bouquets for occasions such as birthdays, anniversaries, sympathy, and get-well, then pay with credit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Amazon Pay, or Afterpay. Distinctive features include BloomSnap photo delivery confirmation and video message cards. BloomNation also runs a florist-facing SaaS side (point-of-sale, website, and order management, now part of Promenade) that powers member shops. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company; no public developer API or documentation program was found during enrichment.

providers.name: FirstCry
providers.description: FirstCry (operated by Brainbees Solutions Ltd) is India's largest omnichannel retailer of baby, kids, and maternity products, founded in 2010 by Supam Maheshwari and Amitava Saha and headquartered in Pune, India. It sells apparel, footwear, toys, diapers, feeding and nursery gear, and personal-care products across its website, mobile apps, and a large network of physical stores, alongside in-house brands such as BabyHug. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and listed publicly on the NSE and BSE in 2024. FirstCry publishes no public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web, policy, and security-disclosure surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Girlboss
providers.description: Girlboss is a community and media brand for ambitious women, positioned as a navigator for the future of work — created to spark the thrill of possibility and to inspire and inform so members can find success on their own terms. Founded by Sophia Amoruso (author of #GIRLBOSS and founder of Nasty Gal), Girlboss grew from editorial content, newsletters, and the Girlboss Rally events into a community brand. Today girlboss.com runs as a Shopify-hosted storefront and brand site. Girlboss was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners; it publishes no first-party developer API, so this profile captures its public web, policy, and agent-facing (llms.txt / well-known) surface rather than an API.

providers.name: PCA SKIN
providers.description: PCA SKIN is a professional skincare brand specializing in dermatologically tested chemical peels and result-oriented corrective products, positioned as a leading professional chemical-peel brand among estheticians and skincare professionals. The brand's direct-to-consumer store at pcaskin.com is built on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface: it implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) with a hosted MCP endpoint plus read-only storefront JSON, so AI shopping agents can discover the catalog, build carts, and drive buyer-approved checkout. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the store's published agent surface (/llms.txt, /.well-known/ucp).

providers.name: appearhere
providers.description: Appear Here is the leading online marketplace for short-term retail space, connecting property owners with brands, designers, and entrepreneurs who want to rent shops, pop-up stores, market stalls, showrooms, and event venues on a flexible, short-term basis. Founded in London in 2014 and backed by Balderton Capital, the two-sided marketplace lets tenants search available space by city and date, book securely online with standardized legal agreements, and message landlords directly, while landlords list and monetize idle retail units. Appear Here operates across the UK, US, and France and has facilitated the opening of more than 10,000 stores for over 250,000 brands and creative entrepreneurs. Appear Here does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its public web, brand, and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: birchbox
providers.description: Birchbox is a beauty and grooming subscription-box retailer that sends members a monthly assortment of personalized deluxe samples across skincare, makeup, haircare, and fragrance, then lets them purchase full-size versions of what they like in its online shop. Originally a New York startup and later acquired, the brand today runs a direct-to-consumer subscription and e-commerce storefront at birchbox.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer program, API, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Buncha
providers.description: Buncha is a scheduled neighborhood grocery delivery service operating across Minnesota and Michigan. Customers shop online from local partner retailers and receive their orders on set weekly routes, with a single refrigerated van consolidating multiple neighbors' orders into one trip for a $3.45 flat delivery fee. Professional personal shoppers hand-pick items into insulated bags, and the aggregated-route model is positioned to cut delivery CO2 emissions by up to 80% versus on-demand services. Buncha is offered through iOS and Android consumer apps and is backed by Foundry Group and Techstars. It is currently a consumer product with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: EDITED
providers.description: EDITED is an AI-powered retail intelligence platform that helps retailers, buyers, merchandisers, planners, designers, and eCommerce teams make data-driven decisions across assortment, pricing, and promotions. Its Market API (the EDITED Data product) exposes a large normalized retail market data set — SKUs, brands, categories, pricing, and assortment signals across thousands of retailers and many countries — so organizations can benchmark against competitors in real time, spot emerging trends early, and integrate competitive intelligence into their own systems. The company is a Seedcamp portfolio company; access to the Market API is sales-gated (demo / contact sales) with no public developer portal or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: ePallet
providers.description: ePallet is an online wholesale marketplace that enables bulk purchasing of a wide variety of products. The platform offers a curated selection of brands and categories, providing real‑time pricing, secure checkout, and hassle‑free delivery coordination. Shoppers can explore brands, business categories, and mixed pallets, while the site emphasizes safe and secure checkout, customer service, and guarantees. ePallet’s mission is to make bulk buying easy and efficient for both consumers and businesses.

providers.name: Amer Sports
providers.description: Amer Sports is a global group of premium sports and outdoor brands with Nordic roots and more than 75 years of history, employing roughly 15,400 people and selling products in over 100 countries. Its portfolio spans ten brands including Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson, Peak Performance, Atomic, Armada, ATEC, DeMarini, EvoShield and Louisville Slugger, covering technical apparel, footwear, winter sports, racquet sports and ball sports equipment. Amer Sports was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). As a consumer sports and outdoor manufacturer it publishes a corporate and investor web presence and a security.txt contact, but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Vastrm
providers.description: Vastrm is a custom-tailored menswear e-commerce company selling made-to-fit polo shirts with 24 different fits and sizes plus additional free adjustments, an online design-your-own configurator, corporate solutions for businesses, and a retail partners program. Vastrm is a Y Combinator and a16z-backed company tracked in the API Evangelist network; it operates a consumer storefront at vastrm.com and publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Weee
providers.description: Weee! is America's largest online Asian grocery store and delivery platform, operating as a direct-to-consumer online supermarket serving major metropolitan areas across the United States. It curates and fulfills inventory through regional distribution centers and cold-chain logistics, bringing together products and ingredients commonly found in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai, Filipino, and Indian supermarkets. The storefront spans fresh produce, frozen meats, seafood, pantry staples, snacks, sauces, hot pot ingredients, beverages, and household essentials, accepts EBT/SNAP in eligible cities, and runs a multilingual experience (English, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese, Thai). Weee is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and the SoftBank Vision Fund. As of this profile Weee publishes no public developer API; this record captures its public web identity and AI-indexing (llms.txt) surface.

providers.name: Blidz
providers.description: Blidz is a membership-based social and gamified e-commerce platform ("Make Money, Save Money, Have Fun") offering deeply discounted deals across grocery, electronics, home goods, and other consumer categories through its iOS and Android shopping apps. Backed by General Catalyst, Blidz operates a consumer mobile marketplace rather than a public developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or public API surface. This APIs.json profile captures the company identity and the security posture of its public web domain.

providers.name: Mayvenn
providers.description: Mayvenn is an Oakland, California beauty-commerce company that sells quality virgin human hair extensions, sew-in weave bundles, closures, frontals, and human hair wigs directly to consumers and through a network of more than 100,000 hair stylists. Founded by Diishan Imira and backed by a16z and 500 Global, Mayvenn pairs its hair products with a stylist-driven distribution model and a 30-day return policy, running its storefront on Shopify at shop.mayvenn.com. The company does not currently publish a public first-party developer API; this profile captures its web identity, security posture, and commercial link surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Qsic
providers.description: Qsic (styled QSIC) is an Australian-founded, AI-driven in-store audio and retail media platform, headquartered in Melbourne with a North American office in Dallas, Texas. The platform blends curated music, targeted audio advertising and store-level intelligence, deploying either over a retailer's existing speaker infrastructure or over premium smart speakers, and adapting playback to ambient conditions, dayparts and shopper behaviour. Qsic sells three connected products — In-Store Audio, Ads and Intelligence — and positions the combination as a way to turn physical stores into measurable retail media networks with store-level performance reporting and demand-side platform integration. Publicly reported deployments include 7-Eleven ("Gulp Radio"), Dollar General, Coles Liquor and Mecca. Qsic runs a live JSON API host at api.getqsic.com and a Vanta-hosted trust center, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification as of this profile.

providers.name: Tiff's Treats
providers.description: Tiff's Treats is an Austin, Texas cookie company founded in 1999 by University of Texas students Tiffany Taylor and Leon Chen, built around warm, baked-to-order cookies delivered same-day. The company operates roughly 90 bakery-storefronts across Texas and the southern and western United States, combining walk-in retail with an owned delivery fleet, an online ordering platform at cookiedelivery.com, and iOS and Android ordering apps. Alongside consumer delivery it runs a substantial corporate gifting, catering, e-gift-card and special-events business, plus an "Elites" subscription membership and a rewards program. Tiff's Treats has raised more than $50 million in outside investment, including a $25 million round led by Morgan Stanley Expansion Capital, and counts Andy Roddick, Brooklyn Decker, Kendra Scott and Dirk Nowitzki among its investors. It is a direct-to-consumer food and delivery operator, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Cado Gifts
providers.description: Cado Gifts, Inc. (CADO Gifting) is a luxury and corporate gifting company operating a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at cadogifting.com, serving the UAE and international markets with curated executive, host, and occasion gift collections plus a corporate/bulk gifting program. The business runs on Shopify (customer accounts, checkout, and blog/journal content) rather than a first-party public API; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No developer program, OpenAPI, or public API documentation is published; the only machine surface discovered is Shopify's Customer Account OIDC/OAuth well-known documents served under the store's own host.

providers.name: Djust
providers.description: DJUST is a French all-in-one, modular B2B commerce platform that helps distributors, wholesalers, manufacturers and retailers launch and automate their B2B eCommerce and eProcurement operations. The platform covers automated order management (24/7 online ordering), AI-assisted quoting with automatic pricing and discounts, integrated online payments with deadline tracking, a conversational AI sales assistant, real-time sales analytics, and prebuilt ERP/CRM integrations. Customers include Eiffage, Auchan Retail and Lesaffre; DJUST reports EUR 1.5B GMV and 2M orders processed in 2025. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Eloquii
providers.description: ELOQUII is a plus-size women's fashion retailer offering trend-driven, fashion-forward apparel and accessories in sizes 14 through 32, including dresses, workwear, outerwear, denim, and occasion wear with frequent seasonal collection refreshes. Known for its fit-obsessed design and inclusive sizing, the brand operates a direct-to-consumer ecommerce storefront at eloquii.com alongside select retail locations. ELOQUII was founded as a plus-size line, acquired by Walmart in 2018, and is now part of FullBeauty Brands. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a consumer ecommerce experience but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: HelprNow
providers.description: HelprNow (operating as Giftr, by Helpr Asia) is Malaysia's leading online gift marketplace, helping people improve relationships with loved ones through a seamless gifting experience. It delivers flowers, cakes, balloons, chocolates, personalised gifts, hampers and gift cards with same-day and nationwide delivery options. The storefront runs on Shopify (helpr-asia.myshopify.com), so its public technical surface is a consumer commerce site rather than a developer API program; the only machine-discoverable interfaces are Shopify's customer-account OAuth2/OpenID Connect endpoints served under giftr.my/.well-known/. Backed by 500 Global; profiled in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: MOO
providers.description: MOO is a London-founded online print and design company that produces premium custom business cards, postcards, flyers, stickers, notebooks, packaging, and branded promotional merchandise for individuals and businesses. Backed by Index Ventures, MOO combines a browser-based design experience with commercial printing, and sells tiered business plans (Business, Advanced, Enterprise) with team management and design services. MOO does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; its developer-style subdomains resolve to the main storefront rather than an API surface. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: WE11DONE
providers.description: WE11DONE (pronounced "well done") is a Seoul-based fashion label founded in 2015 by Dami Kwon and Jessica Jung, the duo behind the Seoul concept boutique Rare Market. The brand fuses late-1990s and early-2000s streetwear and athleisure aesthetics into a globally distributed designer ready-to-wear line, sold through its own e-commerce storefront at we11-done.com and stockists worldwide. Surfaced as a consumer-sector portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 confirmed the company operates a direct-to-consumer retail website but publishes no developer API surface: no developer portal, API reference, well-known metadata, or llms.txt were found.

providers.name: Cabela's
providers.description: Cabela's is a specialty retailer of hunting, fishing, camping, and outdoor recreation merchandise, operating retail stores and an e-commerce platform. Cabela's is a subsidiary of Bass Pro Shops following the 2017 acquisition, and continues to operate under its own brand with retail locations and a consumer-facing web storefront.

providers.name: Caddence
providers.description: Caddence provides a platform to compare golf equipment prices and price history across UK retailers. It aggregates data from over 40 retailers, covering new and used clubs, and updates daily to help golfers find the best deals. The service offers price tracking, historical trends, and alerts, aiming to simplify equipment shopping for enthusiasts and professionals alike.

providers.name: Sonans
providers.description: Sonans is an AI software company building an intelligence layer for fashion merchandising. Its collaborative AI agents replace manual coordination with autonomous workflows that bridge buying decisions and cross-functional execution, turning raw design sketches and purchase orders into production-ready assets including photorealistic product imagery, marketing copy, and catalog data synchronized across ERPs, Shopify, and B2B commerce platforms. Sonans serves fashion brands and designers (streamlining design cycles, asset enrichment, and multi-channel product launches) as well as retailers and merchants (automating assortment planning, catalog enrichment, and inventory management). The company is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Sonans operates a web application at app.sonans.ai but publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: SpartanNash
providers.description: SpartanNash is a Byron Center, Michigan food solutions company that operates as both a wholesale grocery distributor and a retail grocer. Its wholesale segment supplies roughly 2,100 independent retail locations, national accounts and e-commerce partners from a network of distribution centers, and through its MDV business it is the leading distributor of grocery products to United States military commissaries and exchanges worldwide. Its retail segment operates roughly 200 corporate-owned supermarkets under banners including Family Fare, Martin's Super Markets, D&W Fresh Market, VG's Grocery, Dan's Supermarket, Family Fresh Market, Needler's Fresh Market, Fresh City Market, Forest Hills Foods and Supermercado Nuestra Familia, alongside pharmacy and fuel centers. Formed by the 2013 merger of Spartan Stores and Nash Finch, the company traded on Nasdaq as SPTN until C&S Wholesale Grocers completed its acquisition of SpartanNash on September 22, 2025; SpartanNash now operates as part of C&S and its corporate web properties are progressively being folded into cswg.com. SpartanNash publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; supplier and customer system integration is transacted over EDI through trading-partner onboarding rather than a public API.

providers.name: Stockly
providers.description: Stockly (Stockly SAS, headquartered in Vitry-sur-Seine, France) operates a global inventory network for e-commerce, positioning itself as "the first global inventory for Retail." It connects online retailers that are missing stock (Demanders) with brands and official retailers that hold surplus inventory (Suppliers), detecting out-of-stock variants and filling the gaps in real time so that e-shops never run out of stock. Stockly integrates directly with a retailer's e-commerce infrastructure via API, a CMS, or a marketplace, and is building toward a stock exchange for e-commerce inventory in compliance with brands' distribution policies. The company reports 300+ partnered retailers across Europe and 100M+ available items, and is backed by Techstars. Stockly is primarily a partner-onboarded platform rather than a broad self-serve public developer API.

providers.name: ThredUp
providers.description: ThredUp (NASDAQ: TDUP) is one of the world's largest online resale and consignment platforms for secondhand women's and kids' clothing, shoes, and accessories. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Oakland, CA, it lets consumers buy and sell pre-owned fashion via mailed Clean Out Kits, and powers branded recommerce for 60+ retailers through its Resale-as-a-Service (RaaS) platform. ThredUp does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI; RaaS integrations are arranged through its partner sales team, so this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web, engineering, and policy surface rather than a documented API program.

providers.name: Ailumia
providers.description: Ailumia is an AI-driven retail operations platform that helps brands and sellers grow on the world's most valuable marketplaces, with a focus on Amazon. The platform applies artificial intelligence across the retail workflow to manage marketplace sales, inventory, supply chain, and finances, giving operators data-driven guidance and automation to navigate the challenges of modern e-commerce. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Taipei, Taiwan, Ailumia is backed by 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio; enrichment probing found a Cloudflare-fronted WordPress marketing presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Aéropostale
providers.description: An American specialty retailer offering on-trend apparel, accessories, and personal care products targeted at teens and young adults. Operates stores across the United States and internationally through franchise partnerships.

providers.name: Carter's
providers.description: Carter's, Inc. (NYSE: CRI) is the largest branded marketer of young children's apparel in the United States, selling the Carter's, OshKosh B'gosh, Skip Hop and Little Planet brands through its own stores, carters.com and wholesale partners. It is a physical-goods retailer, not a software company, and publishes no developer program: developer.carters.com has no DNS record, www.carters.com/developers is a 404, and api.carters.com — the storefront's backend host — hard-403s every request. Its only external programs are a CJ affiliate program and privately negotiated EDI trading-partner guidelines. No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP server, A2A agent card, SDK or package exists, and none has been authored on its behalf; the placeholder "Carter's API" entry that once stood here has been removed. What it does publish is recorded: a privacy policy with a Global Privacy Control commitment and a OneTrust data-subject request portal, terms, customer service, and its IR newsroom.

providers.name: Dillard's
providers.description: Dillard's, Inc. is a Little Rock, Arkansas department store chain selling apparel, footwear, cosmetics, handbags, menswear and home goods through its stores across the United States and dillards.com. Dillard's publishes no developer program, no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, gRPC or SOAP contract, and no MCP or A2A agent surface — contract discovery on 2026-09-06 found every /.well-known/ and /openapi.json path answering with the storefront single-page-app shell under HTTP 200, matching a nonsense control path.
