providers.name: Genesco
providers.description: Genesco is a specialty retailer and branded company selling footwear, apparel, and accessories through more than 1,400 retail stores and e-commerce sites under banners including Journeys, Schuh, Johnston & Murphy, and Genesco Brands. Genesco publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI document — it says so itself in the llms.txt it serves on journeys.com. What it does publish is an agent-access posture: an llms.txt for AI assistants, a Content-Signal AI-usage declaration in robots.txt on Journeys and Johnston & Murphy, a named allow list for AI search and user-requested agents, an llm= referral attribution convention, and server-rendered schema.org ProductGroup JSON-LD on every product page.

providers.name: Huckberry
providers.description: Huckberry is an American direct-to-consumer online retailer of men's apparel, outdoor gear and lifestyle goods, founded in 2010 by Andy Forch and Richard Greiner and headquartered in San Francisco with offices in Austin and Columbus. It pairs a first-party e-commerce storefront with a large editorial operation — the Huckberry Journal — and an in-house brand portfolio, selling an "everyday adventure" assortment that sits between traditional outdoor retail and menswear. Huckberry is a retailer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable contract. Its public GitHub organization (Huckberry Inc) holds eight repositories, seven of them forks of third-party Ruby e-commerce gems — Solidus AvaTax, Affirm, Paperclip, omniauth-slack — which evidence a self-hosted Ruby storefront rather than a published platform. Partner and affiliate integration is outsourced to the Partnerize network, and customer self-service runs on a Zendesk help center tenant at help.huckberry.com.

providers.name: Jumia
providers.description: Jumia is a pan-African e-commerce company often described as the "Amazon of Africa." Headquartered in Berlin and listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker JMIA since its 2019 IPO, Jumia Technologies AG operates a third-party marketplace, a logistics network (Jumia Logistics), and a digital payments arm (JumiaPay) across eight African markets as of 2026: Egypt, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, and Uganda. The company exited Algeria in February 2026 and previously wound down Cameroon, Gabon, Rwanda, and Tunisia as part of a multi-year restructuring program targeting full-year profitability in 2027. Jumia's commerce platform connects more than 100,000 sellers with consumers across diverse categories including phones and electronics, fashion, home and living, beauty, FMCG, and groceries. Its developer surface is non-trivial: the Jumia Vendor API (vendor center, OAuth 2.0) supports order, inventory, product, and shipment integration for marketplace sellers, while the legacy SellerCenter API (a SellerCenter / Rocket Internet lineage shared with Lazada and Daraz) remains documented with PHP, Python, Ruby, and Node SDKs. JumiaPay exposes a Merchant API for payment creation, verification, refund, recurring-payment agreements, and callback-based webhooks, plus official WooCommerce and Magento payment-gateway plugins. The Jumia GitHub organization is sparse (an open-source playbook, Jumia Tech Blog, and Tech in Porto event site) while the JumiaPay AIG GitHub org hosts the WooCommerce and Magento gateway plugins under Apache 2.0.

providers.name: Radar
providers.description: Radar provides autonomous retail solutions using advanced RFID technology to deliver real-time inventory visibility and checkout automation. Their platform tracks every item in a store with unprecedented speed and location accuracy, enabling instant restocking, precise customer behavior insights, and checkout‑free experiences. By combining high‑precision RFID with AI, Radar aims to transform retail operations, reduce costs, and improve shopper satisfaction across the entire supply chain.

providers.name: Streamlane
providers.description: Streamlane provides an agentic parcel spend management platform for modern operators, helping retailers and 3PLs unify shipping data, automate invoice audits, and optimize network decisions. Their solution reduces parcel spend by 15‑20% through rate benchmarking, network modeling, and contract negotiation insights.

providers.name: 123elec
providers.description: Site officiel 123elec : Boutique en ligne de matériel électrique divers spécialisée dans les installations électriques domestiques et proposant des prix intéressants sur de grandes marques (Legrand, Schneider, Hager, Wago, etc.) sur l'ensemble des équipements et appareillages électriques.

providers.name: Curaleaf Holdings
providers.description: The largest cannabis company in the world by revenue operating cultivation, processing, and retail dispensary operations. Operates in multiple U.S. states and international markets producing cannabis flower, pre-rolls, edibles, and vape products under leading brands.

providers.name: FabFitFun
providers.description: FabFitFun is a members-only lifestyle subscription company that delivers curated seasonal boxes of full-size beauty, fashion, wellness, and home products from premium brands, plus a members' community, customization, and weekly flash-sale shopping. Founded in Los Angeles and backed by 500 Global, Bond Capital, and Kleiner Perkins, FabFitFun serves over one million members with seasonal boxes valued up to $350 for as low as $65 per season. The company operates a direct-to-consumer commerce website, a members' account and box-customization experience, a support/help center, and the FabFitFun Magazine content property. As of this profile FabFitFun publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or API reference; this entry captures its public web and legal surface plus a probed domain-security posture, and remains a portfolio-sourced lead for further enrichment.

providers.name: Thrive Market
providers.description: Thrive Market is a membership-based online grocery retailer headquartered in Marina del Rey, California, selling organic and natural food, pantry staples, frozen meat and seafood, beauty and personal care, baby, pet and household products directly to consumers across the United States. Members pay an annual or monthly fee in exchange for below-retail pricing, and the company operates its own Thrive Market private label alongside thousands of third-party brands. It filters its catalog by diet, ingredient, certification and social value, accepts EBT/SNAP for grocery purchases, and funds free memberships for lower-income families through its Thrive Gives program. Thrive Market is a direct-to-consumer commerce company: it ships a website and mobile apps to shoppers, but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: VideoPoint
providers.description: VideoPoint is a Shopify app from TouchPoints Inc. (a 500 Global portfolio company) that turns a merchant's existing product photos and videos into shoppable, on-site experiences on product-detail and collection pages, with the company reporting an 11-35% conversion uplift and 60-120x ROI from existing content. It is part of the broader TouchPoints suite of AI-powered Shopify apps (alongside TryPoint virtual try-on, plus A/B testing and AI-powered chat) built to engage shoppers, boost conversions, and drive more sales. VideoPoint ships as an embedded Shopify app installed from the Shopify App Store; it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and enrichment lead.

providers.name: HD Supply Holdings
providers.description: HD Supply is one of the largest industrial distributors in North America, providing maintenance, repair, and operations products and value-added services to multifamily, hospitality, healthcare, and government facilities. HD Supply operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of The Home Depot following its acquisition in 2020.

providers.name: Lizee
providers.description: Lizee is a Paris-based Retail-as-a-Service platform that helps brands and retailers launch and operate circular commerce programs — rental, resale, and second-hand — end to end. Its stack pairs a rental platform, a resale/e-commerce platform, and a logistics platform (returns, refurbishment, reverse logistics) behind an operations API so a brand can offer rent or buy-back experiences on top of its existing catalog. Lizee runs a production API (api.lizee.io) and publishes a public Atlassian Statuspage, though it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs — the API surface is partner and integration facing. Lizee was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Speedinvest.

providers.name: Pet Circle
providers.description: Pet Circle is Australia's largest online pet-supplies retailer, selling pet food, flea and worming treatments, toys, bedding and prescription veterinary products direct to consumers across Australia. Founded in mid-2011 in Sydney by Mike Frizell and James Edwards as Paws for Life and rebranded to Pet Circle in early 2014, the company reached unicorn status with a valuation above AU$1 billion after a $125 million Series C in December 2021, and extended into adjacent lines with Pet Circle Pharmacy (petcirclepharma.com.au) and Pet Circle Insurance (petcircleinsurance.com.au, launched May 2023). Its storefront is a headless commerce stack — a commercetools back end fronted by a Vue Storefront / Alokai layer on Vercel, with Google Cloud Functions gluing SaaS services together — but Pet Circle operates that architecture internally: it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable API contract. Trading-partner integration is handled out of band through EDI, and consumer-side partner traffic runs through third-party affiliate networks rather than a first-party API program.

providers.name: ShelterLogic Group
providers.description: ShelterLogic Group is the world leader in shade, shelter, storage, and outdoor lifestyle products with over 70 years of industry experience. Launched in 1991, ShelterLogic develops tough, affordable shelter solutions for everyday consumers and commercial customers. The company operates three manufacturing facilities in the US and China and maintains worldwide distribution. The ShelterLogic brand portfolio includes ShelterLogic, SOJAG, Arrow Storage Products, Quik Shade, CAMP&GO, RIO Beach, and licensed brands including Tommy Bahama, Margaritaville, Life is Good, and Scotts Miracle-Gro. As a B2C manufacturer and retailer, ShelterLogic does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Jolynclothing
providers.description: Jolynclothing is an online retailer specializing in women’s athletic swimwear, offering performance bikinis and one‑piece swimsuits designed for competitive swimming, water polo, and active lifestyles. The brand emphasizes high‑quality materials, functional design, and a commitment to empowering women athletes. Founded with backing from Norwest Venture Partners, Jolynclothing operates a Shopify‑based e‑commerce platform and provides public APIs for product listings, inventory, and order management to support integrations and third‑party developers.

providers.name: TireTutor
providers.description: TireTutor provides an AI‑driven platform that streamlines tire sourcing, estimates, checkout, and repair management. The all‑in‑one solution integrates CRM, inventory, and analytics to help retailers and service centers optimize operations, reduce costs, and improve customer experience through intelligent automation and data‑driven insights.

providers.name: Warby Parker
providers.description: Warby Parker (NYSE: WRBY) is a direct-to-consumer eyewear and vision care company founded in 2010, selling prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, contact lenses, and eye exams online and across 900+ retail stores. It operates a headless, modular commerce architecture and a proprietary point-of-sale system (Point of Everything), plus consumer-facing tools like Virtual Vision Test and PD measurement. Warby Parker does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its API surface (api.warbyparker.com) is internal. The company does publish a public llms.txt for AI agents and an RFC 9116 security.txt with a bug-bounty contact. This API Evangelist profile captures that agent-facing and security posture; there is no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI or SDK surface to harvest.

providers.name: Ace Turtle Services
providers.description: Ace Turtle Services Pvt Ltd (brand "ace turtle") is a Bengaluru, India based retail technology company founded in 2014 that operates a vertical commerce model for international fashion and lifestyle brands. It is the exclusive licensee in India and South Asia for brands including Lee, Wrangler, G-STAR, Toys"R"Us and Dockers, and it runs three proprietary platforms: Rubicon, an omnichannel commerce platform combining distributed order management, inventory, catalogue, pricing and logistics management; Connect App, a store-operations application for in-store fulfilment, helpdesk and visual merchandising; and Albus, a machine-learning layer for inventory optimisation, safety-stock calculation and dynamic markdown. Rubicon is marketed as a channel-agnostic platform that integrates into a brand's existing technology ecosystem, but as of the September 2026 enrichment pass the company publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: CashDro
providers.description: CashDro provides smart cash drawer solutions for businesses, offering secure cash management, card payment integration, and self‑service kiosks. Their products include CashDro7, CashDro5, CashDro4+, and CashDro S, catering to retail, hospitality, and other sectors with hardware and software that ensure safe, efficient cash handling.

providers.name: Chiquita Brands International
providers.description: Chiquita Brands International is a leading global producer, marketer, and distributor of bananas and other fresh produce, recognized worldwide by the iconic Blue Sticker on its bananas. Founded in 1899 as the United Fruit Company and rebranded as Chiquita in 1990, the company is headquartered in Etoy, Switzerland (with significant operations in Fort Lauderdale, Florida) and sources fruit from plantations across Latin America (Honduras, Guatemala, Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia, and Ecuador) for distribution in the United States, Europe, and other markets. Beyond core Cavendish bananas, Chiquita markets specialty banana varieties (organic, Reds, Manzanos, Minis), plantains, pineapples (including the Sunburst Gold variety), and partners with retailers worldwide. Chiquita does not currently publish a consumer-facing developer API; supplier, retailer, and grower integrations are managed through internal portals and bilateral EDI systems, and consumer-facing digital experiences focus on recipes, sticker collection campaigns, and retail merchandising.

providers.name: ApnaMart
providers.description: ApnaMart (Apna Mart) is a Bengaluru-based Indian retail and quick-commerce company founded in 2022 by Chetan Kumar Garg and Abhishek Singh. It operates a network of franchise-model neighborhood grocery and FMCG stores combined with a 15-minute delivery app, serving customers across roughly 14 cities including tier-2 and tier-3 markets such as Ranchi, Hazaribagh, and Bilaspur. Backed by Accel, Peak XV, and Fundamentum, the company blends brick-and-mortar retail with on-demand delivery of daily essentials. ApnaMart is a consumer retail business and does not publish a public developer platform or API surface; this profile in the API Evangelist network captures its identity, domain-security posture, and published web properties.

providers.name: Asleep
providers.description: Asleep is a company identified in the API Evangelist harvest backlog. It appears to be a consumer sleep‑related brand offering products such as eyemasks and pillows via an e‑commerce site. No public API documentation or developer portal could be located despite searching the company’s website and related domains. The profile therefore reflects a lack of discoverable API resources.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble
providers.description: Barnes & Noble is the largest retail bookseller in the United States and the operator of the Nook digital reading platform. Barnes & Noble does not currently publish a public general-purpose developer portal. Trade and affiliate partners integrate through B&N's affiliate program, the B&N Press self-publishing platform for independent authors, EDI-based wholesale channels with publishers, and the Nook content distribution and reading ecosystem.

providers.name: Breadfast
providers.description: Breadfast is an Egyptian quick-commerce and online grocery platform, founded in 2017 in Cairo by Mostafa Amin, Muhammad Habib, and Abdallah Nofal. It delivers groceries, freshly baked bread, dairy, fresh produce, ready-to-eat meals, household essentials, pharmacy, and beauty products — more than 7,000 SKUs — to customers in roughly 60 minutes through a vertically integrated network of dark stores and company-owned bakeries, and also operates Breadfast Pay fintech services. The company serves 300,000+ active users across Cairo, Giza, Alexandria, and Mansoura and processes close to a million orders a month. Breadfast runs a consumer WordPress/WooCommerce marketing site and native iOS/Android apps and does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hershey
providers.description: The Hershey Company is a Fortune 500 confectionery and snacking manufacturer headquartered in Hershey, Pennsylvania, producing Hershey's, Reese's, Kit Kat (US), Jolly Rancher, Ice Breakers, SkinnyPop and Dot's Pretzels across North America and international markets. Hershey is a consumer packaged goods company rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no machine-readable contract. Its public digital surface is the corporate site at thehersheycompany.com, the consumer brand site Hersheyland (hershey.com redirects there), and an investor relations site. This profile records that absence with the probes behind it, alongside press and blog coverage of the company's internal AI and data-platform investment.

providers.name: Keep
providers.description: Keep is an e‑commerce platform powered by Shopify, offering a curated selection of products across various categories. The public website https://keep.com serves as the primary storefront and brand presence. While the site primarily focuses on retail, it represents the company’s digital identity and may expose API endpoints for developers, though none are publicly documented at this time.

providers.name: Miniso
providers.description: MINISO is a global value retailer of lifestyle and consumer products — home goods, accessories, cosmetics, stationery, toys and seasonal items — known for its IP-collaboration merchandise (Harry Potter, PEANUTS, Sanrio, BT21 and others). Founded in Guangzhou, China and publicly listed (NYSE/HKEX), the company operates 7,700+ stores across 112 markets worldwide. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Hillhouse; the public web presence is consumer- and investor-facing and exposes no developer API, developer portal, or partner integration platform at this time.

providers.name: Send4 Tecnologia
providers.description: Send4 Tecnologia (rebranded as After Sale) is a Brazilian post-purchase platform for e-commerce, automating product exchanges, returns, and reverse logistics. Founded in 2017, it has processed over 6 million reverse-logistics transactions and offers intelligent authorization rules for approvals and blocks, a self-service customer exchange portal, real-time returns dashboards, revenue-retention offers (vouchers and cashback), integrated shipping labels and tracking, automated refunds and store credit, and multi-channel WhatsApp and email support. It advertises a simple, flexible API to connect with any e-commerce platform in minutes, though no public developer documentation is currently published. After Sale is now part of the Confi ecosystem alongside Neotrust and the Confi consumer app.

providers.name: Smart & Final Stores
providers.description: Smart & Final Stores is a warehouse-style food and supply retailer operating over 250 stores in the Western United States and 15 stores in northwestern Mexico. The company sells a wide variety of fresh perishables, everyday grocery items, and warehouse-club-sized products to both households and businesses. Smart & Final does not operate a public developer API program but participates in grocery industry digital commerce integrations through third-party platforms.

providers.name: Smartsign
providers.description: Smartsign (SmartSign) is a Brooklyn, New York-based e-commerce retailer of customizable signs, labels, and tags for regulatory, compliance, and safety applications, founded in 1999. It sells pre-designed and custom signage - safety, parking, traffic, property, and facility signs, plus banners and labels - online to businesses of all sizes, including a large share of the Fortune 1000 across education, healthcare, and industrial verticals. Norwest Venture Partners acquired the company in 2019 and Sentinel Capital Partners acquired it in September 2022. SmartSign operates as a business-to-business and business-to-consumer e-commerce storefront and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Smilobaby
providers.description: Smilo (Smilobaby) is a direct-to-consumer baby and toddler products brand founded in 2016 and based in Boston, backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Products are developed by doctors, scientists and engineers and sold direct via smilobaby.com, spanning bottle feeding, pacifiers and teethers, pregnancy and nursing, nursery, mealtime and bath. Its hero products are a pediatric-dentist-designed pacifier that supports a baby's developing palate and a patented-nipple bottle with an extra-sensitive vent that simulates breastfeeding. This is a consumer e-commerce retail brand: it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI, so the enrichment pass records identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: THG
providers.description: THG plc (formerly The Hut Group) is a UK-based consumer brands group founded in 2004 in Manchester and listed on the London Stock Exchange. Following the 2025 demerger of its Ingenuity technology and fulfilment division, THG is a pure-play consumer brands business operating two divisions: THG Beauty (home to Lookfantastic, Cult Beauty, Dermstore and prestige brand partners) and THG Nutrition (led by Myprotein, one of the world's largest online sports-nutrition brands). THG designs, manufactures and sells beauty and nutrition products direct-to-consumer across global markets. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital, an early investor. THG operates corporate, investor-relations and careers web properties but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: THIS
providers.description: THIS™ is a UK plant-based food company making high-protein vegan meat alternatives — including meat-free chicken, bacon, sausages, burgers and mince — sold through major British supermarkets such as Tesco, Sainsbury's, Waitrose, Ocado, Morrisons, Asda and Co-op. Founded in 2019 and backed by Seedcamp, THIS™ is a consumer packaged goods (CPG) brand focused on absurdly tasty plant-based food rather than a developer platform. It operates a marketing and recipe website but publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK at the time of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Bindo
providers.description: Bindo, operating as Bindo Labs, provides a comprehensive cloud‑based point‑of‑sale (POS) platform for hospitality, food‑and‑beverage, and retail businesses. Their solution includes POS terminals, payment processing, inventory management, customer engagement tools, and a suite of integrations for online ordering, gift cards, and analytics. Bindo aims to streamline front‑of‑house and back‑of‑house operations, helping merchants increase sales and improve operational efficiency.

providers.name: Connected Cannabis
providers.description: Connected Cannabis is a retail cannabis brand operating storefronts in Sacramento, Stockton, and San Francisco. The company offers a curated selection of flower, vapes, pre-rolls, extracts, edibles, and merchandise through its online ordering platform. It emphasizes quality, sustainability, and community engagement, providing customers with detailed strain information and a loyalty program. Connected Cannabis aims to enhance the cannabis shopping experience with convenient pickup options and a modern e‑commerce site.

providers.name: Conbini
providers.description: Conbini is a Japanese online retailer offering a wide range of snack foods, confectionery, beverages, and other convenience items. The website conbini.com provides product listings, shopping cart functionality, and account management for customers in Japan. It showcases categories such as candy, chocolates, drinks, and ready‑to‑eat meals, reflecting a typical convenience‑store catalog in an e‑commerce format.

providers.name: OpenStore
providers.description: OpenStore (Miami Labs, Inc. d/b/a OpenStore) is a Miami-based e-commerce holding company that buys direct-to-consumer Shopify businesses from their founders, offering data-driven valuations, offers in as little as 24 hours, and closings in about a week. After acquiring long-tail Shopify merchants, OpenStore uses its own software, marketing, and operations platform to run and grow the brands under one portfolio. Founded in 2021 by Keith Rabois and Atomic's Jack Abraham, OpenStore is backed by General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Atomic, Khosla Ventures, and others. It is a consumer/operator business and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate and web-property surface.

providers.name: Bloomon
providers.description: Bloomon is a flower and gift delivery service that lets customers order one-off bouquets or sign up for a recurring flower subscription delivered on a chosen cadence. It offers seasonal hand-tied and letterbox arrangements, gifting options, gift vouchers, and add-ons, with delivery across the United Kingdom and other European markets. Bloomon is part of the Bloom & Wild Group (confirmed via its published .well-known/security.txt, which points to bloomandwild.com). The company operates a consumer-facing e-commerce and subscription website rather than a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile therefore captures its web, security, and discovery surface rather than a machine-readable API.

providers.name: Clockster
providers.description: Clockster is a frontline staff-management super-app for food & beverage and retail businesses, consolidating attendance and time tracking, shift scheduling, automated payroll, earned wage access, business communication, tasks and checklists into a single mobile-first platform. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Singapore with offices across Kazakhstan and Indonesia, Clockster serves more than 1,300 SMEs across Central and Southeast Asia — including brands such as KFC, Hardee's and Costa Coffee — and is backed by 500 Global, I2BF Global Ventures and Quest Ventures. It is delivered as iOS, Android and Huawei mobile apps plus a web console and currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Fossil Group
providers.description: Fossil Group is a global designer, marketer, and distributor of consumer fashion accessories including watches, jewelry, handbags, small leather goods, belts, and sunglasses sold under owned and licensed brands such as Fossil, Skagen, Michele, Relic, Misfit, and licensed lines for Michael Kors, Diesel, Emporio Armani, Tory Burch, and others.

providers.name: Homzmart
providers.description: Homzmart is a Cairo, Egypt-based online marketplace for furniture, home decor, appliances, and workspace products that connects thousands of local manufacturers, brands, and merchants with consumers across Egypt and the wider MENA region. Founded in 2019 by Mahmoud Ibrahim and Ibrahim Mohamed, the platform lists more than 55,000 products and layers in flexible financing, delivery, and assembly services. Homzmart runs consumer web and mobile storefronts alongside merchant-facing "Sell With Us" and "Homzmart For Business" programs, and has raised roughly $40M in venture funding including a $15M Series A, with 500 Global among its backers. No public developer API program, SDK, or API documentation was found during enrichment; the company publishes a vulnerability-disclosure page and standard trust/policy pages.

1919 (壹玖壹玖 / 1919酒类直供) is a Chengdu-based Chinese alcoholic-beverage retail and supply-chain platform operated by Sichuan 1919 Wines & Spirits SCM Co., Ltd. Founded in 2006, it runs an omnichannel online-to-offline model: the 1919吃喝 consumer app and a third-party e-commerce matrix layered on more than 3,000 franchised stores across 1,000+ Chinese cities, marketed on a 19-minute rapid-delivery promise, alongside a B2B liquor supply-chain business selling order management, logistics and data-marketing services to distributors. The company listed on China's NEEQ board in 2014 (830993), took a RMB 2 billion strategic investment from Alibaba in 2018, and delisted from NEEQ in 2023; its shares now change hands on private secondary marketplaces.

providers.name: A-Frame
providers.description: A-Frame Brands is a Los Angeles-based consumer brand incubator and product-development company founded in 2019 by entrepreneur Ari Bloom and actor Hill Harper. It partners with celebrities and cultural figures to build purpose-driven personal-care, beauty, fragrance, home-care, and pet-care brands, taking each from opportunity identification through product development, design, sourcing, production, and retail go-to-market. Brands in its portfolio include LOVED01 (John Legend), Kinlo (Naomi Osaka), Proudly (Gabrielle Union and Dwyane Wade), and Purrfect Paws, sold through retailers such as Target, Walmart, Amazon, CVS, JCPenney, QVC, and Bath & Body Works. Backed by Initialized Capital. This is a consumer company profile in the API Evangelist network; A-Frame publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: CityMall
providers.description: CityMall is an Indian social-commerce and e-commerce platform operated by Rashanbox Retail Private Limited (CIN U52190HR2020PTC086114), serving Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns through a community-group-buying model. Customers shop across groceries, staples, fashion, electronics, home and kitchen, beauty and health, kids and toys, and books and stationery, with cash-on-delivery and free-delivery options via web and native Android/iOS apps. The company runs on modern web infrastructure (CloudFront CDN, next-gen image optimization) and is backed by Accel, General Catalyst, and Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer API, portal, or documentation surface is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and its verified domain-security posture.

providers.name: NOTHS
providers.description: NOTHS (Not On The High Street, notonthehighstreet.com) is a UK online marketplace that curates and sells unique gifts, jewellery, homeware and personalised products made or sourced by thousands of small UK creative businesses. Founded in 2006 and backed by Index Ventures, the platform connects independent sellers ("partners") with consumers through a curated storefront, seller onboarding, and an affiliate programme. It exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface; its api.notonthehighstreet.com host is a private backend serving the company's own web and mobile storefront. This profile is a VC-portfolio lead enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline via live domain/security probing.

providers.name: Vend
providers.description: Vend was a cloud-based retail point-of-sale and inventory management software company founded in Auckland, New Zealand, backed by investors including Point Nine. Lightspeed announced its acquisition of Vend in March 2021 for approximately US$350 million, and the product lives on as Lightspeed Retail (X-Series). vendhq.com redirects to lightspeedhq.com/vend/, and the former Vend API is documented today at x-series-api.lightspeedhq.com. The X-Series API surface is profiled in the API Evangelist network under the Lightspeed provider, so this profile records the acquired Vend brand rather than duplicating that API.

providers.name: Achats Group
providers.description: Achats Group (아샤그룹) is a South Korean media-commerce company founded in February 2017 and led by CEO Vivian Eun Young Lee, with offices in Pangyo (Seongnam) and Magok (Seoul). It manufactures and sells everyday consumer goods — sanitizing and deodorizing sprays, foot care, living care, health drinks and cosmetics — under its own brands Cellomon, ND247 / Neverdie, Biotreat and BringB, marketing them through short-form video and social advertising that routes buyers into its own Cafe24 storefronts and a Naver Smart Store. Public records put total funding near USD 6.2 million through a Series B. It is a direct-to-consumer consumer-goods business, not a software vendor: as of 2026-09-06 achatsgroup.co.kr is a Cafe24-hosted brochure site still carrying unedited pages from its purchased template, with no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and the brand storefronts are hosted Cafe24 malls whose only /api path is Cafe24's own.

providers.name: Art.com
providers.description: Art.com is a leading online retailer of wall art, canvas prints, framed artwork, photography, and home decor. The platform offers millions of artworks from a wide range of artists and styles, allowing customers to search, customize, and purchase prints for personal or commercial use. It provides tools for framing, matting, and shipping worldwide, and includes features such as AI‑powered search, curated collections, and a marketplace for artists. Art.com serves both individual consumers and businesses looking to decorate spaces with high‑quality art and prints.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble Education
providers.description: Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. (NYSE: BNED) is one of the largest operators of college bookstores in the United States, operating physical and virtual campus stores alongside digital course-materials and educational services. BNED reaches more than 5.7 million students through 1,125+ physical and virtual stores across higher education and K-12 institutions, primarily through its Barnes & Noble College Booksellers subsidiary and the MBS Textbook Exchange wholesale business. Flagship offerings include the First Day and First Day Complete affordable-access course-materials programs, BNC OER+ digital courseware, faculty adoption tools, campus retail and ecommerce services, and BNC AI Tools. BNED separated from Barnes & Noble, Inc. in August 2015 and is not affiliated with the Barnes & Noble retail bookstore chain. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts associated with BNED. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time; integrations with campus systems and learning-management systems are delivered through institutional partnerships rather than a public API surface.

providers.name: Bidit
providers.description: Bidit provides a suite of ecommerce tools that embed directly into online stores, enabling merchants to capture purchase offers from shoppers in real time. The platform offers features such as Bidit Classic, Cart, Onsite Abandonment, Retargeting, Plus, Analytics, and Instore, helping businesses close more sales and improve conversion rates across fashion, footwear, jewellery, gifting, furniture, automotive, and other industries.

providers.name: GlamSt
providers.description: GlamSt (GlamST LLC) builds customized virtual makeover and try-on solutions for beauty brands and retailers, combining augmented reality (AR), artificial intelligence, and machine learning to power virtual makeup and cosmetics try-on across mobile, web, and in-store experiences. Founded with offices in San Francisco, Montevideo (Uruguay), and Wilmington (Delaware), the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. GlamSt was acquired by Ulta Beauty in 2018 and integrated into Ulta's digital innovation team; it exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Tillpoint
providers.description: Tillpoint is a modular, cloud-based EPOS (electronic point of sale) and business management platform for retail, hospitality, and services. A single subscription bundles 25+ modules - Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers/CRM, Staff, Accounting, Purchase Orders, Reporting, and more - across one terminal or thousands of locations. As of this review Tillpoint does not publish a documented public or partner developer API - there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no OpenAPI. Connectivity is delivered through pre-built integrations (QuickBooks Online, Xero, WooCommerce, PayPal, Worldpay, Mailchimp). The API surfaces catalogued here (Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers, Accounting) are logical capability areas of the platform and are honestly marked as endpointsModeled - no endpoints are fabricated. Direct/programmatic access requires contacting Tillpoint.

providers.name: BuyBuddy
providers.description: BuyBuddy is an AI-powered retail merchandising platform positioned as an "AI Merchandiser that tracks, thinks & acts for you." It automates in-store operations for retailers and brands, including planogram compliance and shelf monitoring via computer vision, stockout prevention, product placement optimization, dynamic pricing and promotions, demand forecasting, store transfers, and shopper-behavior analysis through smart tags. BuyBuddy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; at time of enrichment BuyBuddy publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or specification surface, so this remains a company-level profile.

providers.name: Apnaklub
providers.description: Apnaklub is an Indian B2B platform that empowers small retailers by providing access to a wide assortment of FMCG products, credit facilities, free delivery, and other business solutions. It aims to increase retailer profits and reduce risks, serving over 60,000 retailers and 400+ brands, handling more than 1 million annual orders across Tier 2 and 3 markets.

providers.name: Bids.com
providers.description: Bids.com operates an online auction marketplace specializing in jewelry, watches, accessories, and collectibles. The platform offers both auction and fixed-price formats, allowing users to bid on items without registration and purchase instantly after winning. With a wide selection ranging from rings and earrings to art and fashion, Bids.com provides products at significant discounts, often over 80% off retail prices. The site includes comprehensive buyer guides, shipping and return policies, and a dedicated support center, reflecting a fully operational e‑commerce experience.

providers.name: Dupe
providers.description: Dupe.com is a free AI-powered visual search engine and product-comparison platform that finds near-identical, lower-priced alternatives ("dupes") to designer and higher-priced products. Users paste any product URL, upload an image, or type a description, and Dupe's visual matching surfaces similar items from thousands of online retailers at up to 90% less — spanning furniture, home decor, fashion, footwear, beauty, and more. The service also offers AI research reports, room/outfit restyling, a Chrome extension, an iOS app, and a $DUPE rewards program, and it earns revenue through affiliate commissions at no extra cost to users. Dupe additionally operates a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI assistants can search its catalog programmatically. Backed by Kindred Ventures.

providers.name: Sensee
providers.description: Sensee is a French direct-to-consumer online optician and contact-lens retailer, operating since 2005 and run by licensed opticians. It sells contact lenses, lens-care solutions, eye-health products and eyewear across six European markets (France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and Austria) under localized storefronts, and supports third-party insurance payment (tiers payant) via networks such as Kalixia, Santeclair, Almerys and Optilys. Sensee is a subsidiary of Vision Group Holding AG. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no public API, SDK or developer program, only a corporate security.txt / responsible-disclosure surface.

providers.name: Sonic Automotive
providers.description: Sonic Automotive is one of the largest automotive retailers in the United States, operating 100+ franchise dealerships across 13 states representing 25+ automotive brands, and operating EchoPark Automotive used-vehicle stores. The company invests in digital retail, inventory management technology, and automotive data platforms to enhance customer experience across vehicle sales, service, finance, and insurance. Technology partners include Stripe, NETSOL, and CDK Global.

providers.name: VF Corporation
providers.description: VF Corporation is a global apparel and footwear company headquartered in Denver, Colorado. VF owns major brands including Vans, The North Face, Timberland, Altra, Eastpak, Icebreaker, JanSport, Kipling, Napapijri, and Smartwool. The company does not offer a public developer API program; its technology integrations are handled through third-party e-commerce platforms and enterprise supply chain systems. VF Corporation operates more than 1,500 stores globally and integrates with platforms such as Shopify, Amazon, Magento, WooCommerce, and BigCommerce via third-party integration services.

providers.name: Dollar Tree
providers.description: Dollar Tree is a leading operator of discount variety stores in North America, operating more than 16,000 stores under the Dollar Tree and Family Dollar banners. Vendor and supplier integration is primarily handled through EDI, SAP, and ERP systems via the Dollar Tree Vendor Portal. No public REST API is currently available.

providers.name: GOAT
providers.description: GOAT (operated by GOAT Group) is a global online marketplace for authentic sneakers, apparel, and accessories, launched in 2015 and headquartered in the Los Angeles area. The platform pairs a consumer buying-and-selling experience with in-house authentication that verifies new and used footwear and streetwear from thousands of brands, and GOAT Group also operates the Flight Club consignment stores and the alias seller platform. GOAT was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, accel, index-ventures, initialized-capital, matrix-partners, and sv-angel and added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed company profile. It runs a consumer commerce platform rather than a public developer API, so this enriched profile focuses on verified company identity and the security surface probed from its public domain.

providers.name: Mathem
providers.description: Mathem is Sweden's largest pure-play online grocery retailer, delivering fresh food, household goods and pantry staples directly to consumers' homes across Sweden. Customers browse and order the full assortment of a physical supermarket through the mathem.se website and native iOS/Android apps, and receive scheduled home delivery. Mathem merged with the Norwegian online grocer Oda to form one of the Nordics' largest online grocery groups, and its security and careers functions are now operated under the shared Oda organization. Payments are handled through Klarna and the major card networks. Mathem operates a consumer e-commerce storefront and mobile apps; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. This API Evangelist profile was created as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio lead and enriched via the enrichment pipeline; the substantive public technical surface found is an RFC 9116 security.txt and an invite-only YesWeHack bug-bounty program run through Oda.

providers.name: Retailo
providers.description: Retailo (Retailo Technologies) operates a B2B marketplace that helps independent retailers across the MENAP region (Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan) restock their shops, offering thousands of products, instant price comparisons and next-day delivery through the Retailo App. Its ecosystem also includes the Hisaab App, a fintech and bookkeeping product for merchants, and HORECA supply services for the hospitality trade. Founded by Talha Ansari, Muhammad Nowkhaiz and Wahaj Ahmed and backed by 500 Global, the company is operational in markets including the UAE and Pakistan. Retailo distributes its products as native iOS and Android mobile applications and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: Software Solution 24
providers.description: Software Solution 24 appears to be an online retailer specializing in the sale of Microsoft software licenses and related products. The website offers a range of Windows operating system versions, Microsoft Office suites, server CALs, and antivirus solutions, often promoted with significant discounts. Contact information includes a support phone number and email address (support@softwaresolution24.com). The business focuses on providing original Microsoft licenses to customers, positioning itself as a reseller rather than a software development firm.

providers.name: Drop
providers.description: Drop (formerly Massdrop) is a consumer e-commerce brand operated by Corsair that sells limited-edition, community-driven products across mechanical keyboards, audiophile gear, and licensed gaming collaborations (Fallout, Cyberpunk 2077, The Witcher, Call of Duty and others). Founded in San Francisco and backed by Cowboy Ventures and other investors before its acquisition by Corsair, Drop runs a direct-to-consumer storefront at drop.com with a Zendesk-based support helpdesk. It is a retail brand with no public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company in the network.

providers.name: Harvey Norman
providers.description: Harvey Norman is an Australian retail brand for electrical, computers, furniture, bedding and homewares, operated through a franchise system owned by Harvey Norman Holdings Limited (HNHL, ASX: HVN). According to the group's own company overview, HNHL is a public company listed on the Australian Securities Exchange that operates an integrated retail, franchise, property and digital system across eight countries, and owns the Harvey Norman, Domayne and Joyce Mayne trademarks, licensing them to independent franchisees in Australia. The consumer site harveynorman.com.au is fronted by an anti-bot challenge; no public developer portal, API documentation or API contract has been found.

providers.name: SupplyHog
providers.description: SupplyHog is an ecommerce platform built specifically for hardware and building-materials retailers, giving independent hardware and building-supply stores a branded online storefront to sell their products. The platform provides co-op and custom product catalogs, flexible fulfillment (in-store pickup, ship-to-store, local delivery, and ship-to-home with Shippo shipping labels), Stripe-powered payments, TaxJar tax calculation, real-time ERP inventory and pricing synchronization, custom branding and domains, location-aware search, and admin tools for order fulfillment and abandoned-cart recovery. Founded in 2010 as the Nopone.com reverse-auction marketplace, SupplyHog went through the DreamIt and 500 Startups accelerators, pivoted to full ecommerce services, and was acquired by construction-supply retailer R.P. Lumber in 2016. It does not publish a public developer API surface; it acts as a consumer of Stripe, TaxJar, and Shippo.

providers.name: Lexius
providers.description: Lexius is a Y Combinator-backed AI loss-prevention platform that turns a retailer's existing security cameras into proactive, revenue-protecting systems. It detects shoplifting in real time (concealment, product sweeping, known-offender entry), sends instant mobile alerts with video clips, and offers traceback search — natural-language search across every connected camera feed. Lexius also builds case files for law enforcement, flags known offenders chain-wide, and detects slip-and-fall events for liability protection. It connects to existing NVR/VMS systems from any brand, including Hikvision, Axis, Dahua, Hanwha, Bosch, Honeywell, Uniview, Lorex, LTS, Avigilon, and Genetec, and is typically deployed remotely in under 24 hours without replacing hardware. Lexius publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this profile; it is delivered as a hosted dashboard plus camera/NVR integrations.

providers.name: Aday
providers.description: Aday is a direct-to-consumer sustainable fashion brand founded in 2015 in New York City by Nina Faulhaber and Meg He. It designs technical, long-lasting capsule wardrobes built for outfit repetition, using custom recycled fabrics (including post-consumer recycled plastic) and plant-based, beechwood-derived materials produced in closed-loop processes. Aday has raised more than $10 million in venture capital, is backed by Cowboy Ventures, and has been named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, with coverage in Vogue, Refinery29, and Conde Nast Traveler. The company sells globally through its Shopify-powered storefront at thisisaday.com and does not publish a public developer API. This profile was created as an API Evangelist network stub from Cowboy Ventures' portfolio and enriched with company identity and domain-security signals; the storefront returned a Shopify "store is unavailable" lock at the time of the enrichment probe.

providers.name: Capri Holdings
providers.description: Capri Holdings Limited (NYSE: CPRI) is a global luxury fashion group whose portfolio is the Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo brands (Versace was sold to Prada in 2025 and no longer appears on the company's overview). It designs, markets and sells apparel, footwear, handbags and accessories through its own stores, wholesale partners, licensees and brand e-commerce sites. Capri Holdings publishes no developer program: the corporate site at capriholdings.com is a Q4-hosted investor-relations property (news, SEC filings, governance, ESG resources, careers) with no API, documentation, SDK, package, OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or A2A surface, and the api.capriholdings.com and developer.capriholdings.com hosts an earlier scaffold named do not resolve in DNS. Every /.well-known/* path answers with the IR platform's 'Invalid key' catch-all rather than a document. This profile records that absence honestly; nothing has been authored on the company's behalf.

providers.name: Ergo
providers.description: Ergo (ergo Offers, Inc.) is a New York-based e-commerce pricing company that lets online shoppers name their own price. Its flagship product is a Shopify app that adds a "Make an Offer with ergo" button to product pages: a customer submits the price they are willing to pay and how long they are willing to wait, and the merchant accepts or rejects the offer from a backend dashboard. Beyond bartering, Ergo captures true willingness-to-pay data and turns it into pricing analytics and a price-discovery and optimization tool, helping retailers clear excess inventory and reduce blanket discounting. Founded and led by CEO Claire Stepanek (previously supply chain at Apple), Ergo raised a $1.5M pre-seed round in October 2023 led by Anthemis with Wischoff Ventures. Ergo does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity.

providers.name: Percolata
providers.description: Percolata offers AI-based people counting technology for global businesses to comply with COVID-19 occupancy limit laws. It provides predictive analytics to forecast sales and foot traffic, helping organizations optimize staffing and delivery levels. The company leverages machine learning to improve marketing and operations decisions, aiming to increase revenue during the pandemic and beyond.

providers.name: Sephora
providers.description: Sephora is a French multinational chain of personal care and beauty stores and a subsidiary of LVMH, operating 2,700+ locations worldwide and a large ecommerce footprint. Sephora does not publish a public developer API and does not maintain a public GitHub organization. The Sephora storefront and Beauty Insider loyalty program are accessed only through consumer apps and the website; affiliate marketing partnerships are brokered through third-party networks such as Rakuten Advertising and Skimlinks rather than a Sephora-owned API.

providers.name: Bluestem Brands
providers.description: Bluestem Brands, Inc. is an American multi-brand direct-to-consumer retailer headquartered in Eden Prairie, Minnesota. It is best known for Fingerhut, a credit-based catalog and online retailer that extends revolving credit (via partner WebBank) to underserved consumers so they can purchase brand-name merchandise across home, electronics, apparel, and general merchandise categories. Bluestem historically operated a broader portfolio of catalog and e-commerce brands and reaches shoppers through its websites, mobile apps, and printed catalogs. No public developer program, API, or documentation surface was found for Bluestem Brands or Fingerhut at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Bossa Nova Robotics
providers.description: Bossa Nova Robotics develops autonomous retail robots and AI solutions for inventory management. Their flagship robot, Bossa Nova, scans store aisles in Walmart and other retailers, providing real‑time out‑of‑stock detection and analytics. The company shares its technology and learnings through open documentation and APIs to help other businesses build similar automation solutions.

providers.name: Bicycle
providers.description: Bicycle provides AI‑driven analytics agents that enable revenue‑critical teams to query, detect, explain, and act on data directly within their data warehouses such as Snowflake and BigQuery. The platform offers a natural‑language interface, ontology‑based signal patterns, and actionable insights across retail, travel, and Shopify use‑cases, helping businesses replace static dashboards with interactive AI assistants.

providers.name: Digital Brands Group
providers.description: Digital Brands Group (DBG) is a modern retail and technology ecosystem reshaping the shopping experience. It combines apparel brands with a suite of technology tools, leveraging operational expertise to solve logistical challenges, expand addressable markets, and protect brand assets through eCommerce and retail platforms. DBG focuses on direct‑to‑consumer sales, brand authenticity, data security, and enhanced consumer engagement across its portfolio, including the premium denim brand DSTLD.

providers.name: ManoMano
providers.description: ManoMano is Europe's leading online marketplace dedicated to DIY, home improvement and gardening, operating consumer storefronts across France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom plus a ManoManoPro offering for construction professionals and craftsmen. Founded in France and backed by Partech, it connects millions of DIY, tools, heating, electrical, kitchen, bathroom, flooring and garden products from thousands of third-party sellers and brands to individuals and trade buyers. This API Evangelist profile was added as a portfolio-company stub; enrichment found a consumer marketplace with a published llms.txt and help center, but no public developer, seller or partner API surface (no developer portal, OpenAPI, or API subdomain resolves).

providers.name: VANCL
providers.description: VANCL (凡客诚品) is a Chinese direct-to-consumer online apparel brand founded in October 2007 that sells its own-brand men's wear, women's wear, shoes, children's clothing, and home goods through vancl.com and official storefronts on Tmall, JD.com, Douyin, and Youzan. Once China's leading independent B2C fashion retailer, VANCL publishes no public API or developer platform today — its legacy open-platform hosts (open.vancl.com, api.vancl.com) no longer respond. Surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: WON
providers.description: WON is an independent business design and strategic advisory firm serving retail, travel, hospitality, and financial services brands. It provides experience intelligence and operational intelligence to drive profit and growth for its clients, leveraging deep industry expertise and data-driven insights.

providers.name: iPrice
providers.description: iPrice Group is a Southeast Asian e-commerce aggregator and price-comparison platform headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It aggregates billions of live product offers and thousands of coupons from more than a thousand retail partners, letting shoppers compare prices, discover deals, and make more informed purchases across seven markets: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Hong Kong. Backed by 500 Global as part of the Asia Venture Group portfolio, iPrice serves tens of millions of monthly visitors and is known for its large SEA e-commerce dataset. As of this profile, iPrice does not publish a public consumer or partner API, developer portal, or OpenAPI; this record is a company profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Luckypai
providers.description: Luckypai (乐酷天 / LuckyPai Ltd) was a Chinese television home-shopping company founded around 2006-2007 that grew into a leading nationwide TV and online shopping network, selling home appliances, cosmetics, apparel, food, and digital devices. It raised roughly $25M from investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Intel Capital, and the LOTTE Group, and was acquired by Lotte Home Shopping in 2010 for approximately $160M. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As an acquired, no-longer-operating consumer commerce business it has no public developer program, API, or independent web presence; the luckypai.com domain is parked and listed for sale.

providers.name: Prodigy Software
providers.description: Prodigy Software was a San Francisco-based provider of cloud-based automotive retail software, offering a SaaS digital-retailing platform that let car dealerships move the sales process online (web-store services, deal structuring, and financing workflows). Founded in 2015 by Marty Hu and Michia Rohrssen, it raised seed funding from Battery Ventures, SV Angel, 8VC, and CrunchFund, and was acquired by Upstart Holdings in March 2021. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its former domain is parked.

providers.name: Vue
providers.description: Vue (Vue Technology) was an item-level RFID hardware and software company based in Lake Forest, California, backed by Canaan Partners at Series A. Its product family combined RFID readpoints and networking devices with a software platform for real-time, item-level inventory monitoring and tracking, with notable retail rollouts including American Apparel. Tyco's Sensormatic Electronics acquired Vue Technology in October 2008 for approximately $43M, so the company no longer operates as an independent entity. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead; enrichment finds no active developer portal, public API, or first-party artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: Cartame
providers.description: Cartame is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Costco Wholesale
providers.description: Costco Wholesale Corporation is a Fortune 500 American multinational membership-only big-box retail chain that operates warehouse clubs offering a wide selection of merchandise at discounted prices. Costco does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading partner integrations are conducted through EDI and B2B channels using ANSI X12 transactions and the Costco Supplier Portal. Costco operates an e-commerce site, the Costco Travel and Costco Pharmacy properties, and the Costco Photo Center.

providers.name: Diplopia
providers.description: Diplopia is an optometry practice and eyewear retailer based in Richland Center, Wisconsin. The company offers comprehensive eye exams, contact lens services, dry eye treatment, diabetic eye exams, and a curated selection of artisan eyewear. Their mission emphasizes empowering vision and elevating lives through modern eye care, with a focus on community service and innovative eye health solutions.

providers.name: The Bouqs
providers.description: The Bouqs Co. is a direct-from-farm online flower and plant delivery service headquartered in Marina del Rey, California, offering fresh cut bouquets, potted plants, wedding and event florals, and recurring flower subscriptions sourced from sustainable farm partners in South America and California. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech. This is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts. This profile captures verifiable company identity plus live domain-security posture only.

providers.name: CHAGEE Singapore
providers.description: CHAGEE Singapore is a tea brand based in Singapore, offering a wide range of Chinese‑style milk tea, fresh fruit tea, and derivative tea products. Originating from Yunnan, the birthplace of tea, CHAGEE blends traditional tea heritage with modern flavors, operating over 6,000 stores worldwide. The company focuses on original leaf fresh milk tea, integrating oriental culture and innovation to create a new oriental tea shop experience.

providers.name: COSY
providers.description: COSY (CosyRobo) is a retail-technology robotics company that builds autonomous inventory robots for physical stores. Its flagship robot, SCOUT, roams store aisles using AI and machine vision to scan shelves, map products, audit stock levels, and check planogram compliance, feeding the results into a cloud-based management system so retailers can reduce out-of-stocks and improve on-shelf availability. Backed by 500 Global, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it publishes a marketing website but does not currently expose a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Guess
providers.description: Guess? is a global lifestyle brand that designs, markets, distributes, and licenses a leading lifestyle collection of contemporary apparel and accessories for men, women, and children.

providers.name: Hemster
providers.description: Hemster is a fashion-technology company that modernizes tailoring and garment fit through a digital "Fit Profile" system. Customers create a personalized fit pattern once, then match any garment — new or from their existing closet — to that saved profile so it can be tailored to their perfect fit rather than to a standard size. The platform aims to reduce returns, extend the life of clothing people already own, and remove size-related hesitation at purchase, with a sustainability angle around keeping garments out of landfill. Hemster operates a consumer web app at my.hemster.co and a related returns/deadstock product ((re)vive / byrevive.com). It is backed by Bullpen Capital. As of this profile Hemster publishes no public developer, API, or integration surface; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Inkbox
providers.description: Inkbox is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce company selling semi-permanent temporary tattoos. Its proprietary "For Now Ink" formula is made with Genipa plant extract and develops into the skin to last up to about two weeks, longer than surface-level temporary tattoos. Inkbox sells thousands of pre-designed tattoos from independent artists and offers a custom service where customers upload their own artwork to create personalized designs. The business operates as a consumer retail brand with an online store, and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: PetSmart
providers.description: PetSmart is a North American chain of retail stores selling specialty pet supplies, services, and small companion animals. This repository tracks any publicly available APIs, SDKs, and developer resources for PetSmart.

providers.name: The Michaels Companies
providers.description: The Michaels Companies is the largest arts and crafts specialty retailer in North America, providing materials, project ideas, and education for creative inspiration. This repository captures the APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for The Michaels Companies.

providers.name: Minted
providers.description: Minted is a San Francisco-based online design marketplace that crowdsources graphic and fine-art designs from a global community of independent artists and sells the winning work as stationery, wedding invitations, holiday cards, art prints, home decor, and personalized gifts. Its e-commerce storefront at minted.com pairs artist-submitted designs with in-house printing and fulfillment. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; the enrichment pass probed for any public developer surface and found no documented public API — Minted operates as a direct-to-consumer commerce brand, not an API provider.

providers.name: Pep Boys-Manny, Moe & Jack
providers.description: Pep Boys is a leading automotive aftermarket service and retail chain operating service centers and tire and parts stores throughout the United States.

providers.name: Doos
providers.description: Doos is a Saudi-based quick-commerce (q-commerce) platform and mobile app that delivers groceries, fresh produce, beauty, gifting, pharmacy, and lifestyle products in minutes across Saudi Arabia. Founded in 2023 by Tala Al Sahsah, it operates cloud/dark stores in Jeddah and Riyadh with localised assortments, prices, and promotions by city and delivery zone, offering a bilingual (Arabic/English) shopping experience. Doos is backed by 500 Global and received a strategic investment from Jahez to accelerate its expansion in the Kingdom's growing quick-commerce sector. This is a consumer-facing storefront; no public developer program or API has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Home24
providers.description: Home24 is a leading pure-play home & living e-commerce retailer in Continental Europe, founded in Berlin in 2009. It operates across Germany, France, Austria, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Belgium and Italy, selling furniture and home accessories through home24.de and its sister storefronts with a catalog of more than 250,000 products, alongside its own private labels and logistics network. Since April 2023 Home24 SE has been part of the Austrian XXXLutz Group, and it was delisted from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in September 2023. Home24 publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI definition; its programmatic surfaces are a partner/affiliate marketing program and marketplace seller integrations used to syndicate product-data feeds, plus a public engineering blog. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the API-artifact facets are not applicable because there is no public API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Kaufland
providers.description: Kaufland is a German hypermarket chain operating a large network of stores across Europe. It offers a wide range of groceries, household goods, and consumer products both in physical locations and via its online shopping platform. The company provides digital services such as product catalogs, store locators, and e‑commerce APIs for partners, though public API documentation is currently protected by security measures.

providers.name: Augmodo
providers.description: Augmodo provides Spatial AI solutions to augment retail workforces, enabling real‑time inventory tracking across stores. Their platform offers a visual dashboard that helps retailers stay stocked, leveraging computer‑vision and AI to monitor product placement and availability instantly. Clients include major brands such as Amazon, Grammarly, Wyze, Oculus, and others, showcasing broad applicability across e‑commerce and physical retail environments.

providers.name: ICA Gruppen
providers.description: ICA Gruppen is a leading Swedish retail and service conglomerate operating supermarkets, pharmacies, banks, and real estate. It focuses on sustainable growth, digital innovation, and customer convenience across Scandinavia, offering a wide range of products and services while emphasizing environmental responsibility and community engagement.

providers.name: TakeOff
providers.description: Takeoff Technologies, Inc. is an eGrocery micro-fulfillment company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. It paired KNAPP-built robotic storage-and-retrieval hardware with its own cloud software stack — order management, inventory, pick routing, labor management, and delivery orchestration — into micro-fulfillment centers (MFCs) installed inside or beside existing supermarkets, so grocers could assemble online orders in minutes instead of sending shoppers down the aisles. Customers and partners included Albertsons, Wakefern Food Corp., Woolworths Group and Chilean grocer SMU. The company filed for Chapter 11 in May 2024 and Woolworths Group acquired its micro-fulfillment assets in August 2024. Takeoff never published a public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification anywhere on its public surface, and the marketing site at www.takeoff.com no longer serves TLS. A closed API gateway at api.takeoff.com remains live and actively certificate-maintained, serving customer integrations behind authentication.

providers.name: Conrad Electronic
providers.description: Conrad Electronic is a German retailer specializing in electronics, tools, and components for hobbyists, professionals, and makers. It offers a wide range of products including computers, automation, robotics, and DIY supplies through its online store and physical locations across Europe. The company provides APIs for product catalogs, pricing, and order management, supporting integration with e‑commerce platforms and third‑party services.

providers.name: Floward
providers.description: Floward is a leading online flowers and luxury gifting company headquartered in Kuwait and operating across the Middle East and the United Kingdom. Founded in 2017, the company delivers fresh flower arrangements, curated gift boxes, chocolates, cakes, and personalized gifts to more than 40 cities across 9 countries, sourcing blooms daily from ethical growers worldwide and offering same-day and scheduled delivery through its web store and mobile apps. Floward is backed by investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks Floward as a company in the network; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and corporate site but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: Nordstrom
providers.description: Nordstrom is a leading fashion retailer offering compelling clothing, shoes, and accessories for men, women, and children through Nordstrom and Nordstrom Rack stores and online. Nordstrom does not currently operate a public developer portal or expose general-purpose APIs to third-party developers; this repository captures the company profile and any future developer-facing artifacts.

providers.name: Percolata
providers.description: Percolata is a Palo Alto, California predictive-analytics company that applies machine learning to help retailers optimize labor scheduling and marketing spend. Its platform forecasts hourly sales, in-store traffic, and takeout demand to drive staffing optimization and marketing budget allocation, with published claims of 4x higher forecast accuracy, 10-20% same-store sales lift, and a forecast-accuracy guarantee. Named customers include 7-Eleven, Uniqlo, and Telefonica. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Google Ventures (GV). Percolata does not publish a public developer portal or REST API reference; its retail platform is delivered as a managed product with custom application integration. The percolata.com marketing site is now served by Wix, which provisions a live, first-party Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint and an llms.txt for agentic access to public site content.

providers.name: Wolverine World Wide
providers.description: Wolverine World Wide is a leading designer, manufacturer, and marketer of branded footwear, apparel, and accessories. Brands include Merrell, Saucony, Wolverine, Sperry, Sweaty Betty, and Hush Puppies. The company operates global wholesale, direct-to-consumer, and digital commerce channels. Wolverine World Wide does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: CleanCo
providers.description: CleanCo is a United Kingdom-based beverage company, founded in 2019 by Spencer Matthews, that produces premium low- and no-alcohol alternative spirits. Its product line replicates the flavour profiles of traditional spirits across key categories, including CleanGin, CleanRum, CleanVodka and CleanTequila, aimed at consumers who want to reduce alcohol consumption without sacrificing taste. The company sells direct-to-consumer through cleanliquor.com and through grocery and hospitality retail channels across the UK and international markets. CleanCo raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2020. It is a consumer packaged-goods brand and does not publish a developer API, developer portal, or any machine-readable API surface; it is retained in the API Evangelist network only as an identified Lightspeed portfolio company, not as an API provider.

providers.name: Eyewa
providers.description: Eyewa is an online-first eyewear retailer serving the Middle East, selling prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, clear and colored contact lenses, eyewear accessories, and eye-health vitamins through its e-commerce storefront and a network of 260+ physical stores with click-and-collect. Headquartered in Dubai, UAE, Eyewa operates across the GCC and offers regional payment options such as Tabby, Tamara, and Apple Pay. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. Eyewa publishes a consumer storefront, an educational vision-and-eyewear blog, and standard commercial policy pages, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documented API surface.

providers.name: Givemetap
providers.description: GiveMeTap is a UK-based social-enterprise consumer brand that designs and sells reusable, BPA-free stainless-steel and insulated water bottles (500ml and 700ml, plus custom co-branded bottles for businesses). For every bottle sold, GiveMeTap funds five years of clean drinking water for a person in Ghana, giving 20% of its revenue to water projects in Africa; the company reports 116,391 people reached with clean water for life. It operates a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront on the Shopify platform. GiveMeTap is a physical-products company with no first-party developer API, developer portal, or public API documentation; it was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub.

providers.name: HelloFresh
providers.description: HelloFresh SE is a publicly listed (Frankfurt Stock Exchange: HFG), Berlin-headquartered global meal-kit and food-solutions company that ships recipes and pre-portioned ingredients to households across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. Its brand portfolio includes HelloFresh, Factor, Green Chef, EveryPlate, Chefs Plate, Youfoodz, and Good Chop. HelloFresh does not publish a public consumer developer API; its engineering organization is active in open source on GitHub, maintaining widely used infrastructure tooling such as the Janus API gateway, the health-go healthcheck library, and the goengine event-sourcing framework. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and Insight Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: J.C. Penney
providers.description: J.C. Penney Company, Inc. (JCPenney) is an American department store chain offering apparel, accessories, beauty, jewelry, footwear, and home goods. The company emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in late 2020 and continues to operate hundreds of department stores across the United States and Puerto Rico.

providers.name: lovecrafts
providers.description: LoveCrafts (LoveCrafts Group Limited) is a UK-based crafting commerce and community platform — "your home to shop, share and dream in crafts" — selling yarns and fibers, knitting, crochet, sewing, quilting and embroidery patterns, supplies, tools, kits and fabrics, alongside free and paid patterns, tutorials and inspiration content. It operates localized storefronts for North America, the UK, Germany, Australia and France on a Nuxt-based e-commerce stack. LoveCrafts was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. It exposes no public developer portal or API surface; the only machine-discoverable public artifact is an RFC 9116 security.txt with a responsible- disclosure policy (no bug bounty programme).

providers.name: MUSINSA
providers.description: MUSINSA is South Korea's leading online fashion platform, founded in 2001 by Cho Man-ho as a streetwear community and now operating a marketplace that connects more than 10,000 brands with over 16 million members. The company reported roughly USD 3.3 billion in GMV and USD 907 million in revenue for 2024, returned to operating profit, and is pursuing a KOSPI IPO. MUSINSA runs domestic and global storefronts (musinsa.com, global.musinsa.com), a partner/seller program for K-fashion brands, and an engineering organization that publishes on the MUSINSA tech blog. It has raised funding from investors including KKR, Sequoia/Peak XV (formerly Sequoia Capital China / HongShan) and IMM Investment. No genuine public product/developer API or OpenAPI-backed developer portal was found during enrichment; a corporate CMS Swagger UI at dev-api.corp.musinsa.com is an internal tool (its public spec still points at the Swagger petstore demo), so this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Service Properties Trust
